objects.description: Typedef for a UTF-32 code unit stored in an unsigned long. Used with UTF-8/UTF-32 conversion APIs. Size is platform-dependent where unsigned long width varies.

Function pointer type for a thread entry function that takes a single void* argument and returns a void*. On Windows it uses __stdcall, on POSIX the default calling convention. Use with cupsThreadCreate to start a thread.

Opaque thread identifier/handle. On Windows it is a pointer to an internal struct (opaque here). On POSIX it is a pthread_t value. Use with thread control functions such as cupsThreadCreate, cupsThreadCancel, cupsThreadDetach, and cupsThreadWait. Note: the underlying struct _cups_thread_s is only forward-declared here and not defined.

objects.definition:
#if _WIN32
typedef CONDITION_VARIABLE cups_cond_t; // Condition variable
#else
typedef pthread_cond_t cups_cond_t; // Condition variable
#endif
objects.description: Condition variable type for thread synchronization. Wraps CONDITION_VARIABLE on Windows or pthread_cond_t on POSIX. Initialize with cupsCondInit or the platform initializer macro; destroy with cupsCondDestroy. Used with cupsMutexLock/Unlock and cupsCondWait/Broadcast.

objects.definition:
#if _WIN32
typedef CRITICAL_SECTION cups_mutex_t; // Mutual exclusion lock
#else
typedef pthread_mutex_t cups_mutex_t; // Mutual exclusion lock
#endif
objects.description: Mutex type providing mutual exclusion. Wraps CRITICAL_SECTION on Windows or pthread_mutex_t on POSIX. Initialize with cupsMutexInit or platform initializer macro; lock/unlock with cupsMutexLock/Unlock; destroy with cupsMutexDestroy.

objects.definition:
#if _WIN32
typedef SRWLOCK cups_rwlock_t; // Reader/writer lock
#else
typedef pthread_rwlock_t cups_rwlock_t; // Reader/writer lock
#endif
objects.description: Reader-writer lock type. Wraps SRWLOCK on Windows or pthread_rwlock_t on POSIX. Initialize with cupsRWInit; acquire read or write lock with cupsRWLockRead/Write; release with cupsRWUnlock; destroy with cupsRWDestroy.

objects.definition:
#if _WIN32
typedef DWORD cups_thread_key_t; // Thread data key
#else
typedef pthread_key_t cups_thread_key_t; // Thread data key
#endif
objects.description: Thread-local storage key type for associating per-thread data. Wraps DWORD TLS index on Windows or pthread_key_t on POSIX. Access via macros cupsThreadGetData and cupsThreadSetData. Construction API is not provided in this header (initializer macro CUPS_THREADKEY_INITIALIZER is defined as 0).

objects.definition: typedef struct _cups_dir_s cups_dir_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing an open directory stream used by the CUPS directory APIs. The actual structure _cups_dir_s is not defined in this header, making cups_dir_t an incomplete, opaque type intended to be manipulated only via the provided functions (open/read/rewind/close). Details of its contents and lifetime rules beyond using the API are unknown from this header.

Concrete structure describing a single directory entry returned by cupsDirRead. It contains a filename buffer (up to 259 characters plus NUL) and a POSIX stat structure with file metadata for that entry.

objects.definition: typedef struct _cups_dnssd_s cups_dnssd_t;
objects.description: Opaque DNS-SD context object for managing a DNS-SD session within CUPS. Lifetime is managed via cupsDNSSDNew and cupsDNSSDDelete. Internals are intentionally hidden in this header.

objects.definition:
enum cups_dnssd_flags_e			// DNS-SD callback flag values
{
  CUPS_DNSSD_FLAGS_NONE = 0,		// No flags
  CUPS_DNSSD_FLAGS_ADD = 1,		// Added (removed if not set)
  CUPS_DNSSD_FLAGS_ERROR = 2,		// Error occurred
  CUPS_DNSSD_FLAGS_COLLISION = 4,	// Collision occurred
  CUPS_DNSSD_FLAGS_HOST_CHANGE = 8,	// Host name changed
  CUPS_DNSSD_FLAGS_NETWORK_CHANGE = 16,	// Network connection changed
  CUPS_DNSSD_FLAGS_MORE = 128		// More coming
};
typedef unsigned cups_dnssd_flags_t;	// DNS-SD callback flag bitmask
objects.description: Bitmask type for DNS-SD callback flags indicating state and events during browse/query/resolve/service operations. The underlying storage is unsigned; symbolic bits are defined by cups_dnssd_flags_e.

objects.definition:
typedef enum cups_dnssd_rrtype_e	// DNS record type values
{
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_A = 1,		// Host address
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_NS,			// Name server
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_CNAME = 5,		// Canonical name
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_WKS = 11,		// Well known service
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_PTR,		// Domain name pointer
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_TXT = 16,		// One or more text strings
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_RT = 21,		// Router
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_SIG = 24,		// Security signature
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_KEY,		// Security key
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_AAAA = 28,		// IPv6 Address.
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_LOC,		// Location Information.
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_KX = 36,		// Key Exchange
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_CERT,		// Certification record
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_RRSIG = 46,		// RRSIG
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_DNSKEY = 48,	// DNSKEY
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_DHCID,		// DHCP Client Identifier
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_HTTPS = 65,		// HTTPS Service Binding
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_SPF = 99,		// Sender Policy Framework for E-Mail
  CUPS_DNSSD_RRTYPE_ANY = 255		// Wildcard match
} cups_dnssd_rrtype_t;
objects.description: Enumeration of DNS resource record types used with DNS-SD queries and responses. cups_dnssd_rrtype_t is the typedef name for the enum.

objects.definition: typedef struct _cups_dnssd_browse_s cups_dnssd_browse_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing an ongoing DNS-SD browse request. Created with cupsDNSSDBrowseNew and deleted with cupsDNSSDBrowseDelete.

objects.definition: typedef void (*cups_dnssd_browse_cb_t)(cups_dnssd_browse_t *browse, void *cb_data, cups_dnssd_flags_t flags, uint32_t if_index, const char *name, const char *regtype, const char *domain);
objects.description: Function pointer type for browse callbacks invoked for discovered or removed services and related events.

objects.definition: typedef void (*cups_dnssd_error_cb_t)(void *cb_data, const char *message);
objects.description: Function pointer type for error callbacks associated with a cups_dnssd_t context.

objects.definition: typedef struct _cups_dnssd_query_s cups_dnssd_query_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing an ongoing DNS query for a specific fullname/rrtype. Created with cupsDNSSDQueryNew and deleted with cupsDNSSDQueryDelete.

objects.definition: typedef void (*cups_dnssd_query_cb_t)(cups_dnssd_query_t *query, void *cb_data, cups_dnssd_flags_t flags, uint32_t if_index, const char *fullname, uint16_t rrtype, const void *qdata, uint16_t qlen);
objects.description: Function pointer type for query callbacks delivering resource record data for a fullname and rrtype.

objects.definition: typedef struct _cups_dnssd_resolve_s cups_dnssd_resolve_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle for an ongoing DNS-SD resolve operation that turns a service instance into host/port/TXT. Created with cupsDNSSDResolveNew and deleted with cupsDNSSDResolveDelete.

objects.definition: typedef void (*cups_dnssd_resolve_cb_t)(cups_dnssd_resolve_t *res, void *cb_data, cups_dnssd_flags_t flags, uint32_t if_index, const char *fullname, const char *host, uint16_t port, size_t num_txt, cups_option_t *txt);
objects.description: Function pointer type for resolve callbacks providing resolved host, port, and TXT key/value pairs.

objects.definition: typedef struct _cups_dnssd_service_s cups_dnssd_service_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a DNS-SD service registration. Create with cupsDNSSDServiceNew, add records via cupsDNSSDServiceAdd, publish with cupsDNSSDServicePublish, and destroy with cupsDNSSDServiceDelete.

objects.definition: typedef void (*cups_dnssd_service_cb_t)(cups_dnssd_service_t *service, void *cb_data, cups_dnssd_flags_t flags);
objects.description: Function pointer type for service registration callbacks reporting publication state and errors.

objects.definition: typedef struct _cups_array_s cups_array_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a CUPS sorted array. The struct body is not defined in this header, indicating it is an internal/private type managed via the provided API. Instances are created and managed through the cupsArray* functions. Details of memory layout and fields are intentionally hidden.

objects.definition: typedef int (*cups_array_cb_t)(void *first, void *second, void *data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for array comparison callbacks. Returns an int less than, equal to, or greater than zero to order elements; the third parameter is user-supplied data. Used to define sort/ordering for cups_array_t.

objects.definition: typedef size_t (*cups_ahash_cb_t)(void *element, void *data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for array hashing callbacks. Returns a hash value for an element; the second parameter is user-supplied data. Enables hashed lookup behavior for cups_array_t when provided to cupsArrayNew.

objects.definition: typedef void *(*cups_acopy_cb_t)(void *element, void *data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for array element copy callbacks. Should allocate/duplicate and return a copy of the given element; the second parameter is user-supplied data. Used by cups_array_t to own element copies when provided to cupsArrayNew.

objects.definition: typedef void (*cups_afree_cb_t)(void *element, void *data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for array element free callbacks. Should release resources for an element previously stored in the array; the second parameter is user-supplied data. Used by cups_array_t for element destruction when provided to cupsArrayNew.

functions.name: cupsAddDest
functions.signature: extern size_t cupsAddDest(const char *name, const char *instance, size_t num_dests, cups_dest_t **dests) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Adds (or updates) a destination entry in a dynamically managed array of cups_dest_t and returns the new count. Typical usage: grow a destinations array discovered via cupsGetDests or built manually.
requirements: dests must be a valid pointer to a cups_dest_t* variable; if *dests is non-NULL it must point to memory allocated by CUPS destination APIs or compatible with their reallocation semantics.
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
instance may be NULL or a NUL-terminated string.
num_dests must match the current number of entries in *dests.
Caller must later free the array with cupsFreeDests when no longer needed.

functions.name: cupsAddDestMediaOptions
functions.signature: extern size_t cupsAddDestMediaOptions(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *dinfo, unsigned flags, cups_media_t *media, size_t num_options, cups_option_t **options) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Adds media-related IPP options for the given destination and media selection to an options array. Useful for configuring media size, source, type, and margins according to printer capabilities.
requirements: dest must point to a valid destination as returned by cupsGetDests/cupsGetNamedDest.
dinfo should be obtained for dest via cupsCopyDestInfo; may be required to resolve capabilities.
media must point to a populated cups_media_t structure to drive option generation.
options must be a valid pointer to a cups_option_t*; will be reallocated as needed.
num_options must be the current count of entries in *options.
flags is a bitfield of cups_media_flags_t; only documented values should be used.
http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or a valid HTTP connection for the destination.
Caller must free options with cupsFreeOptions when done.

functions.name: cupsAddIntegerOption
functions.signature: extern size_t cupsAddIntegerOption(const char *name, long value, size_t num_options, cups_option_t **options) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Adds/updates a single integer-valued option to an options array, returning the new count.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
options must be a valid pointer to a cups_option_t*; may be reallocated.
num_options must reflect the current number of entries in *options.
Caller must free options with cupsFreeOptions when done.

functions.name: cupsAddOption
functions.signature: extern size_t cupsAddOption(const char *name, const char *value, size_t num_options, cups_option_t **options) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Adds/updates a single string option to an options array, returning the new count.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
value must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string for string-valued options.
options must be a valid pointer to a cups_option_t*; may be reallocated.
num_options must match the current number of entries in *options.
Caller must free options with cupsFreeOptions when done.

functions.name: cupsAreCredentialsValidForName
functions.signature: extern bool cupsAreCredentialsValidForName(const char *common_name, const char *credentials);
functions.description: Checks whether the provided X.509 credentials are valid for the given common name. Returns true if valid. Intended for validating TLS/identity credentials used by CUPS.
requirements: common_name must be a NUL-terminated string naming the expected identity.
credentials must reference a credentials bundle/path or data in the format expected by CUPS (exact format not specified in this header).
Returns a boolean; caller should handle false as invalid.

functions.name: cupsCancelDestJob
functions.signature: extern ipp_status_t cupsCancelDestJob(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, int job_id) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Requests cancellation of a specific job on a destination. Returns an IPP status code.
requirements: http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or a valid HTTP connection to the server hosting dest.
dest must be a valid destination.
job_id must be a job identifier previously created/returned by CUPS for dest.
Caller must check the returned ipp_status_t for success/failure.

functions.name: cupsCheckDestSupported
functions.signature: extern bool cupsCheckDestSupported(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *info, const char *option, const char *value) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Checks whether a given option/value pair is supported by the specified destination according to its capabilities.
requirements: dest must be a valid destination; info should normally be a cups_dinfo_t for dest (from cupsCopyDestInfo).
option must be a non-NULL option name; value must be a non-NULL string value.
http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or an open connection.
Returns true if supported; caller should handle false as unsupported.

functions.name: cupsCloseDestJob
functions.signature: extern ipp_status_t cupsCloseDestJob(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *info, int job_id) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Finalizes/closes a previously created job on a destination, indicating no further documents will be sent. Returns IPP status.
requirements: job_id must be a valid job created via cupsCreateDestJob.
dest must be valid and match the job.
info should be capability info for dest (from cupsCopyDestInfo).
http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or a valid connection.
Caller must check return status.

functions.name: cupsConcatString
functions.signature: extern size_t cupsConcatString(char *dst, const char *src, size_t dstsize) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Appends src to dst ensuring NUL-termination within dstsize. Returns the length of the concatenated string (similar to strlcat semantics).
requirements: dst must be a writable buffer of size dstsize bytes.
src must be a NUL-terminated string (may be empty).
dstsize must be the total size of dst in bytes; if 0, no writing occurs.
Caller must ensure buffers do not overlap in undefined ways beyond standard strcat semantics.

functions.name: cupsConnectDest
functions.signature: extern http_t *cupsConnectDest(cups_dest_t *dest, unsigned flags, int msec, int *cancel, char *resource, size_t resourcesize, cups_dest_cb_t cb, void *user_data) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Establishes an HTTP connection to the server or device backing a destination. Optionally returns the resource path and reports progress via callback. Returns an http_t* or NULL on failure.
requirements: dest must be a valid destination.
flags is a cups_dest_flags_t bitfield; use documented values (e.g., CUPS_DEST_FLAGS_DEVICE).
msec is a timeout in milliseconds; non-negative; 0 may mean default.
cancel may be NULL or point to an int that, when set non-zero, cancels the attempt.
resource must be a writable buffer of size resourcesize bytes if non-NULL; resourcesize must reflect its size.
cb may be NULL or a valid cups_dest_cb_t; user_data is passed to the callback.
Caller must close the returned http_t* using the appropriate HTTP API when done.

functions.name: cupsCopyCredentials
functions.description: Loads/copies credentials for the given common name from a path into memory, returning a pointer to the credential data/string. Ownership of the returned memory is with the caller.
requirements: path must identify a credentials store or directory understood by CUPS.
common_name must be a NUL-terminated string.
Caller must free the returned string using the appropriate deallocator (unspecified here; typically free()).
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check.

functions.name: cupsCopyCredentialsKey
functions.description: Loads/copies the private key associated with the credentials/common name from the given path into memory. Returns a dynamically allocated string/buffer.
requirements: path and common_name must be valid strings.
Caller must free the returned memory and handle NULL on failure.
Key format is implementation-defined; treat as opaque.

functions.name: cupsCopyCredentialsPublicKey
functions.description: Loads/copies the public key for the given common name from the credentials store at path into memory.
requirements: path and common_name must be valid strings.
Caller must free the returned memory and handle NULL on failure.

functions.name: cupsCopyCredentialsRequest
functions.description: Loads/copies a stored certificate signing request (CSR) for the given common name from path. Returns a dynamically allocated string or NULL.
requirements: path and common_name must be valid strings.
Caller must free the returned memory and handle NULL on failure.

functions.name: cupsCopyDest
functions.signature: extern size_t cupsCopyDest(cups_dest_t *dest, size_t num_dests, cups_dest_t **dests) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Appends a copy of the provided destination to an array of destinations, returning the new count. Useful for building a list programmatically.
requirements: dest must point to a valid cups_dest_t to copy.
dests must be a valid pointer to a cups_dest_t* that may be reallocated.
num_dests must equal the current number of entries in *dests.
Caller must free with cupsFreeDests.

functions.name: cupsCopyDestInfo
functions.description: Fetches and returns a capability/status information object for a destination (cups_dinfo_t).
requirements: dest must be valid.
http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or a live connection.
dflags is a cups_dest_flags_t bitfield; use documented values.
Caller must free the returned cups_dinfo_t with cupsFreeDestInfo.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check.

functions.name: cupsCopyDestConflicts
functions.signature: extern int cupsCopyDestConflicts(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *info, size_t num_options, cups_option_t *options, const char *new_option, const char *new_value, size_t *num_conflicts, cups_option_t **conflicts, size_t *num_resolved, cups_option_t **resolved) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Analyzes option constraints for a destination when adding a new option/value, returning conflicting and auto-resolved options. Helps validate/adjust job options.
requirements: dest and info must refer to the same destination; info typically from cupsCopyDestInfo.
options must point to an array of num_options entries (may be 0/NULL).
new_option and new_value must be non-NULL strings to check.
num_conflicts/conflicts and num_resolved/resolved may be non-NULL to receive results; provided pointers will be allocated by the function and must be freed with cupsFreeOptions.
http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or a valid connection.
Caller must check the return int for success as defined by implementation (not specified here).

functions.name: cupsCopyString
functions.signature: extern size_t cupsCopyString(char *dst, const char *src, size_t dstsize) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Copies src into dst with NUL-termination up to dstsize bytes. Returns the length of src (similar to strlcpy semantics).
requirements: dst must be a writable buffer of size dstsize bytes (dst may be NULL only if dstsize==0).
src must be a NUL-terminated string.
dstsize is the total capacity of dst; if 0, no writing occurs.

functions.name: cupsCreateCredentials
functions.signature: extern bool cupsCreateCredentials(const char *path, bool ca_cert, cups_credpurpose_t purpose, cups_credtype_t type, cups_credusage_t usage, const char *organization, const char *org_unit, const char *locality, const char *state_province, const char *country, const char *common_name, const char *email, size_t num_alt_names, const char * const *alt_names, const char *root_name, time_t expiration_date) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Creates new X.509 credentials (certificate and key), optionally as a CA certificate, and stores them under path. Supports specifying purposes, key type, usage, subject fields, SANs, root/issuer, and expiration.
requirements: path must indicate a writable credentials location.
common_name must be provided as a subject CN.
purpose, type, usage must be valid enum values.
If ca_cert is true or root_name is used, appropriate permissions and CA context must exist (details unspecified here).
If num_alt_names > 0, alt_names must point to an array of that length.
expiration_date specifies validity end; must be a valid time_t.
Returns false on failure; caller must check.

functions.name: cupsCreateCredentialsRequest
functions.signature: extern bool cupsCreateCredentialsRequest(const char *path, cups_credpurpose_t purpose, cups_credtype_t type, cups_credusage_t usage, const char *organization, const char *org_unit, const char *locality, const char *state_province, const char *country, const char *common_name, const char *email, size_t num_alt_names, const char * const *alt_names) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Generates a certificate signing request (CSR) and private key and stores them under path for the given subject and parameters.
requirements: path must be writable.
purpose, type, usage must be valid enumerations.
common_name must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
If num_alt_names > 0, alt_names must be a valid array pointer of that length.
Returns false on failure; caller must check.

functions.name: cupsCreateDestJob
functions.signature: extern ipp_status_t cupsCreateDestJob(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *info, int *job_id, const char *title, size_t num_options, cups_option_t *options) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Creates a new print job on a destination with the provided title and options, returning the assigned job_id. Returns an IPP status.
requirements: http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or a valid connection to dest.
dest must be valid; info should correspond to dest.
job_id must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the new ID.
title should be a NUL-terminated job title (may be NULL/unspecified depending on implementation).
If num_options > 0, options must point to an array of that length.
Caller must check ipp_status_t for success before using job_id.

functions.name: cupsCreateTempFd
functions.signature: extern int cupsCreateTempFd(const char *prefix, const char *suffix, char *filename, size_t len) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Creates a secure temporary file and returns an open file descriptor. Optionally returns the filename created within the provided buffer.
requirements: prefix and suffix may be NULL or strings used to influence the filename (implementation-defined).
If filename is non-NULL, it must point to a writable buffer of size len bytes; len must be sufficient to hold the generated path including NUL.
Returns -1 on failure; caller must close the returned FD on success.

functions.name: cupsCreateTempFile
functions.signature: extern cups_file_t *cupsCreateTempFile(const char *prefix, const char *suffix, char *filename, size_t len) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Creates a secure temporary file and returns an open cups_file_t handle. Optionally returns the filename.
requirements: If filename is non-NULL, it must be a writable buffer of size len bytes.
prefix/suffix may guide naming; semantics implementation-defined.
On success, caller must close the returned cups_file_t via CUPS file API; returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cupsDoAuthentication
functions.signature: extern bool cupsDoAuthentication(http_t *http, const char *method, const char *resource) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Performs client-side authentication (e.g., HTTP or OAuth) for a given HTTP method and resource on the connection. Returns true if authentication succeeded or was not required.
requirements: http must be a valid HTTP connection.
method must be a valid HTTP method string (e.g., "GET", "POST").
resource must be a valid resource path string.
Caller must handle false as an authentication failure and possibly retry per server challenge.

functions.name: cupsDoFileRequest
functions.signature: extern ipp_t *cupsDoFileRequest(http_t *http, ipp_t *request, const char *resource, const char *filename) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Sends an IPP request with a file as the document payload to the server at the specified resource. Returns the IPP response message.
requirements: http must be a valid connection.
request must be a valid IPP request object; caller retains ownership.
resource must be a valid IPP endpoint path.
filename must refer to a readable file path.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check and free the returned ipp_t when done.

functions.name: cupsDoIORequest
functions.signature: extern ipp_t *cupsDoIORequest(http_t *http, ipp_t *request, const char *resource, int infile, int outfile) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Sends an IPP request with I/O file descriptors for input/output data streaming. Returns the IPP response.
requirements: http must be a valid connection.
request must be a valid IPP request object.
resource must be a valid path.
infile may be -1 (no data) or an open FD positioned at the start of the data to send.
outfile may be -1 (discard) or an open FD for receiving data.
Caller must manage FDs and free returned ipp_t; NULL indicates failure.

functions.name: cupsDoRequest
functions.description: Sends a plain IPP request (no document data) to the given resource and returns the IPP response.
requirements: http must be valid.
request must be a valid IPP message; caller retains ownership until call returns.
resource must be a valid path.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must free the returned ipp_t.

functions.name: cupsEncodeOption
functions.signature: extern ipp_attribute_t *cupsEncodeOption(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group_tag, const char *name, const char *value) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Encodes a single option name/value into an IPP message under the specified attribute group, returning the created/updated attribute.
requirements: ipp must be a valid ipp_t* for the request being built.
group_tag must be a valid IPP group tag (e.g., IPP_TAG_JOB).
name and value must be non-NULL strings.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cupsEncodeOptions
functions.signature: extern void cupsEncodeOptions(ipp_t *ipp, size_t num_options, cups_option_t *options, ipp_tag_t group_tag) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Encodes an array of options into the given IPP message under the specified group tag.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
If num_options > 0, options must point to an array of that length.
group_tag must be a valid IPP group tag.
No return value; caller must ensure ipp remains valid.

functions.name: cupsEnumDests
functions.signature: extern bool cupsEnumDests(cups_dest_flags_t flags, int msec, int *cancel, cups_ptype_t type, cups_ptype_t mask, cups_dest_cb_t cb, void *user_data) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Enumerates available destinations asynchronously/synchronously, invoking the callback for each discovered or updated destination until timeout or cancellation. Returns true on success.
requirements: cb must be a non-NULL callback function; user_data is passed through.
msec is the enumeration timeout in milliseconds; 0 may indicate an immediate/one-shot query.
cancel may be NULL or point to an int set non-zero to cancel.
flags is a cups_dest_flags_t mask controlling behavior.
type/mask filter destinations by cups_ptype_t.
Caller must be prepared to handle multiple callback invocations and track flags like CUPS_DEST_FLAGS_MORE.

functions.name: cupsFindDestDefault
functions.signature: extern ipp_attribute_t *cupsFindDestDefault(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *dinfo, const char *option) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Returns the IPP attribute representing the default value for a given option for the destination.
requirements: dest and dinfo must be valid and correspond.
option must be a non-NULL string.
http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or a valid connection.
Returns NULL if not found.

functions.name: cupsFindDestReady
functions.signature: extern ipp_attribute_t *cupsFindDestReady(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *dinfo, const char *option) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Returns the IPP attribute representing the current ready value (e.g., media-ready) for the given option on the destination.
requirements: dest and dinfo must be valid and correspond.
option must be non-NULL.
http may be default or valid connection.
Returns NULL if not available.

functions.name: cupsFindDestSupported
functions.signature: extern ipp_attribute_t *cupsFindDestSupported(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *dinfo, const char *option) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Returns the IPP attribute listing supported values for the given option on the destination.
requirements: dest and dinfo must be valid and correspond.
option must be non-NULL.
http may be default or valid connection.
Returns NULL if not available.

functions.name: cupsFinishDestDocument
functions.description: Signals the end of a document being sent to a job on a destination (paired with cupsStartDestDocument and data writes). Returns IPP status.
requirements: A job must have been created and a document started with cupsStartDestDocument.
http must be valid (or default) for dest.
dest and info must be valid and correspond.
Caller must check return status.

functions.name: cupsFormatString
functions.signature: extern ssize_t cupsFormatString(char *buffer, size_t bufsize, const char *format, ...) _CUPS_FORMAT(3,4) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Formats a string into buffer using printf-style formatting, writing at most bufsize bytes including NUL. Returns number of bytes that would have been written (like snprintf).
requirements: buffer must be a writable memory region of size bufsize bytes (or NULL if bufsize==0).
format must be a valid NUL-terminated format string; variadic args must match.
bufsize is the total capacity, including space for NUL.
Caller should handle truncation based on return value.

functions.name: cupsFormatStringv
functions.signature: extern ssize_t cupsFormatStringv(char *buffer, size_t bufsize, const char *format, va_list ap) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: va_list variant of cupsFormatString. Returns the number of bytes that would have been written.
requirements: buffer, bufsize, and format constraints are the same as cupsFormatString.
ap must be an initialized va_list matching format.

functions.name: cupsFreeDestInfo
functions.description: Frees a cups_dinfo_t previously obtained via cupsCopyDestInfo.
requirements: dinfo may be NULL (no effect) or a valid pointer previously returned by cupsCopyDestInfo.
Must not be used after free.

functions.name: cupsFreeDests
functions.description: Frees an array of destinations previously allocated/managed by CUPS destination APIs.
requirements: If num_dests > 0, dests must point to an array of that many entries allocated by CUPS APIs.
Safe to pass num_dests==0 with NULL pointer.

functions.name: cupsFreeJobs
functions.description: Frees an array of job records returned by cupsGetJobs.
requirements: If num_jobs > 0, jobs must point to an array of that many entries returned by cupsGetJobs.
Safe to call with 0/NULL.

functions.name: cupsFreeOptions
functions.description: Frees an options array returned or built with CUPS option APIs.
requirements: If num_options > 0, options must point to an array of that many entries allocated by CUPS option functions.
Safe to call with 0/NULL.

functions.name: cupsGetClock
functions.description: Returns a high-resolution monotonic clock value in seconds (implementation-defined) for timing purposes.
requirements: No arguments. The value is for relative timing; not a wall-clock time.

functions.name: cupsGetCredentialsExpiration
functions.description: Returns the expiration time of the provided credentials as a time_t, or 0/(time_t)-1 on error depending on implementation.
requirements: credentials must identify a credentials object/path understood by CUPS.
Caller must interpret special values per implementation (not specified here).

functions.name: cupsGetCredentialsInfo
functions.signature: extern char *cupsGetCredentialsInfo(const char *credentials, char *buffer, size_t bufsize) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Writes a human-readable summary of the credentials into buffer and returns buffer, or NULL on failure.
requirements: credentials must reference valid credentials.
buffer must be a writable memory region of size bufsize bytes.
bufsize must be sufficient for summary text or result may be truncated/NULL.

functions.name: cupsGetCredentialsTrust
functions.signature: extern http_trust_t cupsGetCredentialsTrust(const char *path, const char *common_name, const char *credentials, bool require_ca) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Evaluates the trust level of credentials for common_name against trust anchors found at path. Optionally requires CA presence. Returns an http_trust_t classification.
requirements: path must point to a credential store/path containing trust anchors/certs.
common_name must be a NUL-terminated string.
credentials must specify the cert/chain to evaluate.
Caller must handle the returned trust classification appropriately.

functions.name: cupsGetDefault
functions.description: Returns the name of the default destination/printer for the current server/user context, or NULL if none.
requirements: http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or a valid connection.
Returned pointer is managed by CUPS; treat as read-only and copy if needed.

functions.name: cupsGetDest
functions.signature: extern cups_dest_t *cupsGetDest(const char *name, const char *instance, size_t num_dests, cups_dest_t *dests) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Finds and returns a pointer to a destination within an existing array by name/instance, or NULL if not found.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL string; instance may be NULL.
dests must point to an array of num_dests entries.
Returned pointer refers into the provided array; do not free individually.

functions.name: cupsGetDestMediaByIndex
functions.signature: extern bool cupsGetDestMediaByIndex(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *dinfo, size_t n, unsigned flags, cups_media_t *media) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Retrieves the nth media option for a destination according to flags and writes it to media. Returns true on success.
requirements: dest and dinfo must be valid and correspond.
n is a zero-based index less than the media count (use cupsGetDestMediaCount).
media must point to a writable cups_media_t.
flags is a cups_media_flags_t mask.
http may be default or a valid connection.

functions.name: cupsGetDestMediaByName
functions.signature: extern bool cupsGetDestMediaByName(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *dinfo, const char *name, unsigned flags, cups_media_t *media) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Looks up a media by name (e.g., PWG media keyword) and writes details to media. Returns true on success.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL media name string.
dest/dinfo must be valid and correspond.
media must be writable.
flags is a cups_media_flags_t mask.
http may be default or valid connection.

functions.name: cupsGetDestMediaBySize
functions.signature: extern bool cupsGetDestMediaBySize(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *dinfo, int width, int length, unsigned flags, cups_media_t *media) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Finds a media matching the requested size (in hundredths of millimeters) according to flags and writes details to media. Returns true on success.
requirements: width and length are integers in hundredths of millimeters; must be positive to find a match.
dest/dinfo must be valid and correspond.
media must be writable.
flags is a cups_media_flags_t mask.
http may be default or valid connection.

functions.name: cupsGetDestMediaCount
functions.signature: extern size_t cupsGetDestMediaCount(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *dinfo, unsigned flags) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Returns the number of media entries available for the destination given the flags.
requirements: dest/dinfo must be valid and correspond.
flags is a cups_media_flags_t mask.
http may be default or valid connection.

functions.name: cupsGetDestMediaDefault
functions.signature: extern bool cupsGetDestMediaDefault(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *dinfo, unsigned flags, cups_media_t *media) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Retrieves the default media for the destination according to flags and writes it to media. Returns true on success.
requirements: dest/dinfo must be valid and correspond.
flags is a cups_media_flags_t mask.
media must point to a writable cups_media_t.
http may be default or valid connection.

functions.name: cupsGetDestWithURI
functions.description: Constructs a destination object for a printer/device identified by name and URI. Useful for ad-hoc device connections.
requirements: name and uri must be non-NULL strings.
Returned cups_dest_t* must be freed with cupsFreeDests(1, ptr) or an appropriate API (implementation-dependent).
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cupsGetDests
functions.description: Retrieves the list of available destinations from the server/environment and returns the count, storing the array in *dests.
requirements: dests must be a valid pointer to cups_dest_t*; will be allocated by the function and must be freed with cupsFreeDests.
http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or a valid connection.

functions.name: cupsGetEncryption
functions.description: Returns the current default HTTP encryption setting used by CUPS for new connections.
requirements: No arguments. Use to inspect current policy.

functions.name: cupsGetError
functions.description: Returns the last IPP error/status encountered by the calling thread in CUPS APIs.
requirements: No arguments. Caller must interpret the ipp_status_t per IPP specs.

functions.name: cupsGetErrorString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the last IPP error/status.
requirements: Return pointer is managed by CUPS; treat as read-only and copy if needed.

functions.name: cupsGetFd
functions.signature: extern http_status_t cupsGetFd(http_t *http, const char *resource, int fd) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Performs an HTTP GET for a resource and writes the response body to the provided file descriptor. Returns an HTTP status.
requirements: http must be a valid connection.
resource must be a valid path.
fd must be a writable, open file descriptor.
Caller must check the http_status_t and manage the FD lifecycle.

functions.name: cupsGetFile
functions.signature: extern http_status_t cupsGetFile(http_t *http, const char *resource, const char *filename) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Performs an HTTP GET for a resource and writes the response body to the specified file path. Returns an HTTP status.
requirements: http must be a valid connection.
resource must be a valid path.
filename must be a writable file path; parent directory must exist and be writable.
Caller must check returned status.

functions.name: cupsGetIntegerOption
functions.signature: extern long cupsGetIntegerOption(const char *name, size_t num_options, cups_option_t *options) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Looks up an option by name in an options array and returns its value as a long (parsed from string).
requirements: name must be non-NULL.
If num_options > 0, options must point to an array of that length.
Caller must handle cases where the option is not found or not an integer (return semantics implementation-defined).

functions.name: cupsGetJobs
functions.signature: extern size_t cupsGetJobs(http_t *http, cups_job_t **jobs, const char *name, bool myjobs, cups_whichjobs_t whichjobs) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Retrieves a list of jobs from the server, optionally filtered by destination name, ownership, and state. Returns the number of jobs and stores the array in *jobs.
requirements: jobs must be a valid pointer to cups_job_t*; on success, the function allocates the array which must be freed with cupsFreeJobs.
name may be NULL (all) or a specific destination name.
myjobs indicates whether to restrict to the current user.
whichjobs selects the subset per cups_whichjobs_t.
http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or a valid connection.

functions.name: cupsGetNamedDest
functions.signature: extern cups_dest_t *cupsGetNamedDest(http_t *http, const char *name, const char *instance) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Gets a single destination by name/instance from the server/environment. Returns a dynamically allocated cups_dest_t or NULL.
requirements: name must be non-NULL; instance may be NULL.
http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or a valid connection.
Caller must free the returned destination using cupsFreeDests(1, dest).

functions.name: cupsGetOption
functions.signature: extern const char *cupsGetOption(const char *name, size_t num_options, cups_option_t *options) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Finds and returns the string value for an option in an options array, or NULL if not found.
requirements: name must be non-NULL.
If num_options > 0, options must point to an array of that length.
Returned pointer refers to internal storage owned by the options array; do not free.

functions.name: cupsGetPassword
functions.signature: extern const char *cupsGetPassword(const char *prompt, http_t *http, const char *method, const char *resource) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Obtains a password from the application/user via the configured password callback, possibly using the prompt and connection context. Returns a pointer to a password string.
requirements: prompt must be a non-NULL string.
http may be a valid connection (used for context) or NULL/CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT.
method and resource provide context for authentication.
Returned pointer is managed by CUPS/callback; treat as read-only and copy immediately if needed.

functions.name: cupsGetRand
functions.description: Returns a random unsigned value from CUPS' RNG facility.
requirements: No arguments. Not cryptographically strong unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: cupsGetResponse
functions.description: Receives and parses an IPP response from the server for the given resource after a prior request was sent. Returns an ipp_t or NULL.
requirements: http must be a valid connection with a pending IPP response.
resource must match the endpoint used.
Caller must free the returned ipp_t.

functions.name: cupsGetServer
functions.description: Returns the current default server hostname/URI string used by CUPS.
requirements: No arguments. Returned pointer is managed by CUPS; do not free.

functions.name: cupsGetUser
functions.description: Returns the current default user name used by CUPS.
requirements: No arguments. Returned pointer is managed by CUPS; do not free.

functions.name: cupsGetUserAgent
functions.description: Returns the current default User-Agent string used by CUPS HTTP requests.
requirements: No arguments. Returned pointer is managed by CUPS; do not free.

functions.name: cupsHashData
functions.signature: extern ssize_t cupsHashData(const char *algorithm, const void *data, size_t datalen, unsigned char *hash, size_t hashsize) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Computes a hash of data using the specified algorithm and writes the raw digest into hash buffer. Returns the number of bytes written or a negative value on error.
requirements: algorithm must name a supported hash (e.g., "sha256"); exact names unspecified here.
data must point to a buffer of length datalen bytes.
hash must be a writable buffer of size at least hashsize; hashsize must be >= required digest length for the algorithm.
Caller must check the return value for success and digest length.

functions.name: cupsHashString
functions.signature: extern const char *cupsHashString(const unsigned char *hash, size_t hashsize, char *buffer, size_t bufsize) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Converts a raw hash value into a printable string (e.g., hex) stored in buffer and returns buffer.
requirements: hash must point to the raw digest bytes of length hashsize.
buffer must be writable with capacity bufsize; must be large enough for the encoded representation plus NUL.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cupsHMACData
functions.signature: extern ssize_t cupsHMACData(const char *algorithm, const unsigned char *key, size_t keylen, const void *data, size_t datalen, unsigned char *hash, size_t hashsize) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Computes an HMAC over data using the specified algorithm and key, writing the raw MAC to hash. Returns number of bytes written or negative on error.
requirements: algorithm must be a supported HMAC/hash algorithm name.
key must point to keylen bytes of key material.
data/datalen must specify the input message.
hash/hashsize must be large enough for the algorithm's MAC size.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: cupsLocalizeDestMedia
functions.signature: extern const char *cupsLocalizeDestMedia(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *info, unsigned flags, cups_media_t *media) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Returns a localized (human-readable) string for the specified media selection for a destination.
requirements: dest/info must be valid and correspond.
media must point to a valid cups_media_t selection to localize.
flags is a cups_media_flags_t mask.
http may be default or valid connection.
Returned string pointer is managed by CUPS; treat as read-only.

functions.name: cupsLocalizeDestOption
functions.signature: extern const char *cupsLocalizeDestOption(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *info, const char *option) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Returns a localized (human-readable) label for an option for the destination.
requirements: dest/info must be valid and correspond.
option must be non-NULL.
http may be default or valid connection.
Returned pointer is managed by CUPS; read-only.

functions.name: cupsLocalizeDestValue
functions.signature: extern const char *cupsLocalizeDestValue(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *info, const char *option, const char *value) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Returns a localized (human-readable) label for a specific option value for the destination.
requirements: dest/info must be valid and correspond.
option and value must be non-NULL.
http may be default or valid connection.
Returned pointer is managed by CUPS; read-only.

functions.name: cupsLocalizeNotifySubject
functions.description: Generates a localized subject line for a CUPS/IPP notification event in the specified language. Returns a newly allocated string.
requirements: lang must be a valid language object (may be NULL for default).
event must be a valid IPP event/notification message.
Caller must free the returned string; NULL indicates failure.

functions.name: cupsLocalizeNotifyText
functions.description: Generates localized body text for a CUPS/IPP notification event. Returns a newly allocated string.
requirements: lang may be NULL or a valid cups_lang_t*.
event must be a valid IPP event message.
Caller must free the returned string; NULL indicates failure.

functions.name: cupsParseOptions
functions.signature: extern size_t cupsParseOptions(const char *arg, const char **end, size_t num_options, cups_option_t **options) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Parses a string of option assignments into an options array, returning the new count. Supports parsing until end pointer if provided.
requirements: arg must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string containing options in supported syntax (implementation-defined).
end may be NULL or receives a pointer to the position after the parsed input.
options must be a pointer to a cups_option_t*; may be reallocated.
num_options must match the current number of entries in *options.
Caller must free options with cupsFreeOptions.

functions.name: cupsPutFd
functions.signature: extern http_status_t cupsPutFd(http_t *http, const char *resource, int fd) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Performs an HTTP PUT/POST of the data from fd to the given resource. Returns HTTP status.
requirements: http must be a valid connection.
resource must be a valid path.
fd must be an open, readable file descriptor positioned at the start of data.
Caller must check returned status.

functions.name: cupsPutFile
functions.signature: extern http_status_t cupsPutFile(http_t *http, const char *resource, const char *filename) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Performs an HTTP PUT/POST of the data from a file at filename to the given resource. Returns HTTP status.
requirements: http must be valid.
resource must be a valid path.
filename must refer to a readable file.
Caller must check returned status.

functions.name: cupsReadResponseData
functions.signature: extern ssize_t cupsReadResponseData(http_t *http, char *buffer, size_t length) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Reads raw response/document data from the server into buffer, up to length bytes. Returns number of bytes read or negative on error.
requirements: http must be a valid connection with data available to read.
buffer must be writable with capacity length bytes.
length must be > 0 to read data.

functions.name: cupsRemoveDest
functions.signature: extern size_t cupsRemoveDest(const char *name, const char *instance, size_t num_dests, cups_dest_t **dests) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Removes a destination (name/instance) from an array of destinations, returning the new count. May shrink/reallocate the array.
requirements: name must be non-NULL; instance may be NULL.
dests must be a valid pointer to cups_dest_t* that may be reallocated.
num_dests must equal the current number of entries in *dests.
Caller must free with cupsFreeDests when array no longer needed.

functions.name: cupsRemoveOption
functions.signature: extern size_t cupsRemoveOption(const char *name, size_t num_options, cups_option_t **options) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Removes an option by name from an options array, returning the new count.
requirements: name must be non-NULL.
options must be a valid pointer to cups_option_t* that may be reallocated.
num_options must reflect current count in *options.
Caller must free with cupsFreeOptions when done.

functions.name: cupsSaveCredentials
functions.signature: extern bool cupsSaveCredentials(const char *path, const char *common_name, const char *credentials, const char *key) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Saves the provided credentials and associated private key for the given common name into the store at path. Returns true on success.
requirements: path must be writable and point to a credential store location.
common_name must be a NUL-terminated string.
credentials and key must reference the proper certificate/key material in formats expected by CUPS.
Caller must check boolean return.

functions.name: cupsSendRequest
functions.signature: extern http_status_t cupsSendRequest(http_t *http, ipp_t *request, const char *resource, size_t length) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Initiates sending an IPP request to the server at resource, optionally indicating the length of document data to follow (for subsequent write calls). Returns HTTP status.
requirements: http must be a valid connection.
request must be a valid IPP request object.
resource must be a valid path.
length is the size of the document data to follow or CUPS_LENGTH_VARIABLE for chunked/unknown length (per CUPS).
Caller must check returned status and then use cupsWriteRequestData to send document bytes, followed by cupsGetResponse to receive the IPP response.

functions.name: cupsSetClientCredentials
functions.signature: extern bool cupsSetClientCredentials(const char *credentials, const char *key) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Sets the client TLS credentials (certificate and private key) to use for subsequent connections/requests. Returns true on success.
requirements: credentials and key must reference the appropriate cert/key material in formats expected by CUPS.
Call before establishing connections that require client auth.
Affects process/thread global CUPS state; use carefully in multithreaded contexts (details unspecified).

functions.name: cupsSetDefaultDest
functions.signature: extern void cupsSetDefaultDest(const char *name, const char *instance, size_t num_dests, cups_dest_t *dests) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Marks a destination in an existing array as the default by name/instance.
requirements: name must be non-NULL; instance may be NULL.
dests must point to an array of num_dests destinations.
No return value; if destination is not found, no change occurs (behavior unspecified here).

functions.name: cupsSetDests
functions.signature: extern bool cupsSetDests(http_t *http, size_t num_dests, cups_dest_t *dests) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Saves the provided list of destinations to the server or user configuration. Returns true on success.
requirements: dests must point to an array of num_dests destinations.
http may be CUPS_HTTP_DEFAULT or a valid connection.
May require appropriate permissions to modify server/user configuration.

functions.name: cupsSetEncryption
functions.description: Sets the default encryption mode for future HTTP connections in CUPS.
requirements: e must be a valid http_encryption_t value.
Affects subsequent connections; existing connections unaffected.

functions.name: cupsSetOAuthCB
functions.description: Registers an OAuth token callback used to obtain tokens during authenticated requests. The cb_data is passed to the callback.
requirements: cb may be NULL to clear; otherwise must match cups_oauth_cb_t signature.
cb must remain valid for the duration of its use (typically process lifetime or until replaced).

functions.name: cupsSetPasswordCB
functions.description: Registers a password callback used by CUPS to prompt/retrieve passwords when needed. cb_data is passed through.
requirements: cb may be NULL to clear; otherwise must match cups_password_cb_t signature.
Callback must be thread-safe if used in multithreaded contexts (not specified; recommended).

functions.name: cupsSetServer
functions.description: Sets the default CUPS server (hostname/URI) for future operations.
requirements: server must be a NUL-terminated string specifying hostname or URI accepted by CUPS.
Affects global/default context for subsequent calls.

functions.name: cupsSetServerCredentials
functions.signature: extern bool cupsSetServerCredentials(const char *path, const char *common_name, bool auto_create) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Configures the server’s TLS credentials store/path and identity (common_name). Optionally creates missing credentials automatically. Returns true on success.
requirements: path must be a valid directory/path for server credentials.
common_name must be a NUL-terminated string.
If auto_create is true, process must have permissions to create credentials under path.

functions.name: cupsSetUser
functions.description: Sets the default user name used by CUPS for job submissions and authorization.
requirements: user must be a NUL-terminated string.
Affects subsequent operations for the current process.

functions.name: cupsSetUserAgent
functions.description: Sets the default User-Agent string for HTTP requests made by CUPS.
requirements: user_agent must be a NUL-terminated string.
Affects subsequent HTTP requests initiated after this call.

functions.name: cupsSignCredentialsRequest
functions.signature: extern bool cupsSignCredentialsRequest(const char *path, const char *common_name, const char *request, const char *root_name, cups_credpurpose_t allowed_purpose, cups_credusage_t allowed_usage, cups_cert_san_cb_t cb, void *cb_data, time_t expiration_date) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Signs a certificate signing request (CSR) using a CA found at path/root_name, restricting purpose/usage and optionally validating SANs via callback. Stores resulting certificate in the credentials store. Returns true on success.
requirements: path must point to a credentials store containing the CA (root_name).
common_name must match/identify the subject for storage.
request must reference the CSR to sign (format unspecified here).
allowed_purpose and allowed_usage restrict the CSR; must be valid masks.
cb may be NULL or a function to validate subjectAltName entries; cb_data is passed through.
expiration_date sets the certificate validity end.
Caller must check boolean return.

functions.name: cupsStartDestDocument
functions.signature: extern http_status_t cupsStartDestDocument(http_t *http, cups_dest_t *dest, cups_dinfo_t *info, int job_id, const char *docname, const char *format, size_t num_options, cups_option_t *options, bool last_document) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Starts sending a new document for a job to the destination with the specified document name, MIME format, and options. Returns HTTP status; data is written via cupsWriteRequestData, and completion via cupsFinishDestDocument.
requirements: http must be a valid connection.
dest and info must be valid and correspond.
job_id must be a valid job created by cupsCreateDestJob for this dest.
docname may be NULL or a NUL-terminated name; format must be a valid MIME type string (e.g., CUPS_FORMAT_PDF).
If num_options > 0, options must point to an array of that length.
last_document indicates whether more documents will follow for the job.
On success, caller must stream data using cupsWriteRequestData and then call cupsFinishDestDocument.

functions.name: cupsWriteRequestData
functions.signature: extern http_status_t cupsWriteRequestData(http_t *http, const char *buffer, size_t length) _CUPS_PUBLIC;
functions.description: Writes document data bytes to the current HTTP/IPP request previously started (e.g., by cupsSendRequest or cupsStartDestDocument). Returns HTTP status.
requirements: http must be a valid connection with an active request expecting data.
buffer must point to at least length bytes; length may be 0 for no-op.
Caller should repeat until all data is sent and check each returned status.

functions.name: ippAddBoolean
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddBoolean(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, const char *name, bool value);
functions.description: Adds a single boolean IPP attribute with the given name to the specified IPP message in the provided group.
requirements: ipp must be a valid, initialized ipp_t* created by ippNew/ippNewRequest/ippNewResponse.
group must be a valid attribute group tag (e.g., IPP_TAG_OPERATION, IPP_TAG_JOB, IPP_TAG_PRINTER, etc.).
name must be a non-NULL, non-empty attribute name following IPP naming rules.
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes (typically prior to encoding/sending).

functions.name: ippAddBooleans
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddBooleans(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, const char *name, size_t num_values, const bool *values);
functions.description: Adds a multi-valued boolean IPP attribute to the given IPP message/group.
requirements: ipp must be a valid, initialized ipp_t*.
group must be a valid attribute group tag for insertion.
name must be a non-NULL, non-empty attribute name.
values must be non-NULL when num_values > 0; num_values specifies the number of boolean values.
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddCollection
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddCollection(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, const char *name, ipp_t *value);
functions.description: Adds a single collection-valued IPP attribute (begin/end collection with contained members) to the given message/group.
requirements: ipp must be a valid, initialized ipp_t*.
group must be a valid attribute group tag for insertion.
name must be a non-NULL, non-empty attribute name.
value must be a valid ipp_t* representing a collection (attributes within it form the collection members).
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddCollections
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddCollections(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, const char *name, size_t num_values, const ipp_t **values);
functions.description: Adds a multi-valued collection attribute to the given message/group.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
name must be a non-NULL, non-empty attribute name.
values must point to an array of num_values collection ipp_t*; for num_values > 0, values must be non-NULL and each element must point to a valid collection object.
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddCredentialsString
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddCredentialsString(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, const char *name, const char *credentials);
functions.description: Adds a credentials string attribute to the given IPP message/group. Used for attributes carrying opaque credential data as text.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
credentials must be a non-NULL string appropriate for the target attribute; length must fit IPP text/keyword limits for the attribute type (unknown exact constraints).
Call only when the IPP message allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddDate
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddDate(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, const char *name, const ipp_uchar_t *value);
functions.description: Adds a single date/time (IPP_TAG_DATE) attribute to the given message/group.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
value must point to a valid IPP date/time encoding (11 bytes per IPP spec; actual size handling internal).
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddInteger
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddInteger(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, ipp_tag_t value_tag, const char *name, int value);
functions.description: Adds a single integer or enum attribute (value_tag IPP_TAG_INTEGER or IPP_TAG_ENUM) to the given message/group.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
value_tag must be a valid integer-compatible tag (commonly IPP_TAG_INTEGER or IPP_TAG_ENUM).
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
value must be in the valid range for the target attribute as defined by IPP/implementation (exact constraints unknown).
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddIntegers
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddIntegers(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, ipp_tag_t value_tag, const char *name, size_t num_values, const int *values);
functions.description: Adds a multi-valued integer or enum attribute to the given message/group.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
value_tag must be a valid integer-compatible tag (e.g., IPP_TAG_INTEGER or IPP_TAG_ENUM).
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
values must be non-NULL when num_values > 0; each value must be valid for the attribute (exact constraints unknown).
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddOctetString
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddOctetString(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, const char *name, const void *data, size_t datalen);
functions.description: Adds a single octetString (raw bytes) attribute to the given message/group.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
If datalen > 0, data must be non-NULL; datalen should not exceed IPP_MAX_OCTETSTRING (1023) for a single value.
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddOutOfBand
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddOutOfBand(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, ipp_tag_t value_tag, const char *name);
functions.description: Adds an out-of-band value attribute (e.g., unknown, no-value, not-settable) with the specified value tag to the given group.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
value_tag must be an out-of-band tag such as IPP_TAG_UNKNOWN, IPP_TAG_NOVALUE, IPP_TAG_NOTSETTABLE, IPP_TAG_DELETEATTR, or similar as appropriate.
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddRange
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddRange(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, const char *name, int lower, int upper);
functions.description: Adds a single rangeOfInteger value attribute to the given message/group.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
lower and upper define the inclusive range; typically lower <= upper (caller should supply a valid range).
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddRanges
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddRanges(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, const char *name, size_t num_values, const int *lower, const int *upper);
functions.description: Adds a multi-valued rangeOfInteger attribute to the given message/group using parallel arrays of lower and upper bounds.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
For num_values > 0, lower and upper must be non-NULL arrays of length num_values; each pair should form a valid range (typically lower[i] <= upper[i]).
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddResolution
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddResolution(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, const char *name, ipp_res_t units, int xres, int yres);
functions.description: Adds a single resolution attribute to the given message/group with specified units and X/Y resolutions.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
units must be a valid ipp_res_t (IPP_RES_PER_INCH or IPP_RES_PER_CM).
xres and yres must be positive integers appropriate for the attribute.
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddResolutions
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddResolutions(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, const char *name, size_t num_values, ipp_res_t units, const int *xres, const int *yres);
functions.description: Adds a multi-valued resolution attribute to the given message/group using arrays for X/Y resolutions.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
units must be a valid ipp_res_t.
For num_values > 0, xres and yres must be non-NULL arrays of length num_values; each element must be a positive integer.
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddSeparator
functions.description: Adds a group separator (IPP_TAG_ZERO) attribute to the IPP message to delimit groups when needed.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
Call only when structuring raw attribute streams where a separator is meaningful.

functions.name: ippAddString
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddString(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, ipp_tag_t value_tag, const char *name, const char *language, const char *value);
functions.description: Adds a single string attribute (e.g., text, name, keyword, uri, charset, language, etc.) with the specified value tag to the given message/group.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
value_tag must be a valid string-compatible tag (e.g., IPP_TAG_TEXT, IPP_TAG_NAME, IPP_TAG_KEYWORD, IPP_TAG_URI, IPP_TAG_CHARSET, IPP_TAG_LANGUAGE, IPP_TAG_MIMETYPE).
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
value must be a non-NULL string valid for the chosen value_tag and within the IPP-defined length limits for that type (e.g., IPP_MAX_TEXT, IPP_MAX_NAME, IPP_MAX_URI, etc.).
language may be NULL unless value_tag requires language; when provided it should be a valid naturalLanguage code.
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddStringf
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddStringf(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, ipp_tag_t value_tag, const char *name, const char *language, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Adds a single formatted string attribute using printf-style formatting into a value of the specified string value_tag.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
value_tag must be a valid string-compatible tag.
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
format must be a non-NULL printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.
The resulting formatted string must meet the IPP length/character constraints for the chosen value_tag.
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddStringfv
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddStringfv(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, ipp_tag_t value_tag, const char *name, const char *language, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: Adds a single formatted string attribute using a va_list for arguments, for the specified string value_tag.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
value_tag must be a valid string-compatible tag.
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
format must be non-NULL; ap must be an initialized va_list matching the format.
Result must meet IPP length/character constraints for the chosen value_tag.
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAddStrings
functions.signature: ipp_attribute_t *ippAddStrings(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_tag_t group, ipp_tag_t value_tag, const char *name, size_t num_values, const char *language, const char * const *values);
functions.description: Adds a multi-valued string attribute (of the specified string value_tag) to the given message/group.
requirements: ipp must be valid and initialized.
group must be a valid group tag.
value_tag must be a valid string-compatible tag.
name must be non-NULL and non-empty.
For num_values > 0, values must be non-NULL pointing to an array of num_values C strings; each string must meet IPP constraints for the chosen value_tag.
language may be NULL unless the value_tag implies a language.
The IPP message must be in a state that allows adding attributes.

functions.name: ippAttributeString
functions.description: Formats the given attribute’s value(s) as a human-readable string into buffer and returns the number of bytes that would be written (like snprintf semantics).
requirements: attr must be a valid attribute pointer.
If buffer is non-NULL, it must point to a writable memory region of size at least bufsize bytes.
bufsize should reflect the size of buffer; if buffer is NULL, bufsize may be used to query needed size (exact NULL handling unknown).

functions.name: ippContainsInteger
functions.description: Checks whether the integer-valued attribute contains the specified integer (useful for multi-valued integer/enum attributes).
requirements: attr must be a valid attribute pointer of an integer-compatible type (IPP_TAG_INTEGER or IPP_TAG_ENUM).

functions.name: ippContainsString
functions.description: Checks whether the string-valued attribute contains the specified string value (useful for multi-valued string attributes).
requirements: attr must be a valid attribute pointer of a string-compatible type.
value must be a non-NULL C string for comparison.

functions.name: ippCopyAttribute
functions.description: Copies a single attribute into the destination IPP message. When quickcopy is true, implementation may reuse storage (const/copy-on-write) where possible.
requirements: dst must be a valid, initialized destination ipp_t*.
attr must point to a valid attribute from an existing IPP message.
quickcopy controls copy behavior; callers must not modify reused storage unless the library ensures safety.
The destination message must allow adding attributes.

functions.name: ippCopyAttributes
functions.signature: bool ippCopyAttributes(ipp_t *dst, ipp_t *src, bool quickcopy, ipp_copy_cb_t cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Copies selected or all attributes from src IPP message to dst. An optional callback can filter which attributes to copy. quickcopy may enable shallow/const copies.
requirements: dst and src must be valid, initialized ipp_t* objects.
If cb is non-NULL, it will be called for each attribute to decide copying; cb_data is passed through.
The destination must be in a state that allows adding attributes.
Callers must not modify attributes that are shallow-copied via quickcopy in ways that violate library ownership semantics (exact behavior depends on implementation).

functions.name: ippCopyCredentialsString
functions.description: Returns a newly-allocated copy of a credentials string value from the given attribute.
requirements: attr must be a valid attribute pointer containing a credentials string.
The returned string must be freed by the caller using the appropriate deallocation function (typically free).

functions.name: ippCreateRequestedArray
functions.description: Creates and returns a cups_array_t of requested attribute names for a request, typically from the 'requested-attributes' attribute.
requirements: request must be a valid IPP request object.
The caller is responsible for freeing the returned array using the cups_array_t API.

functions.name: ippDateToTime
functions.description: Converts an IPP date/time byte array (IPP_TAG_DATE encoding) to a time_t value.
requirements: date must point to a valid IPP date/time encoding (11 bytes per IPP specification).

functions.name: ippDelete
functions.description: Deletes/frees an IPP message object and all associated resources.
requirements: ipp must be a pointer previously returned by ippNew/ippNewRequest/ippNewResponse.
Do not use the ipp pointer after calling this function.

functions.name: ippDeleteAttribute
functions.description: Removes the specified attribute from the IPP message and frees it.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.
attr must be an attribute currently belonging to ipp.
After deletion, attr becomes invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: ippDeleteValues
functions.signature: bool ippDeleteValues(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, size_t element, size_t count);
functions.description: Deletes one or more values from a (possibly multi-valued) attribute starting at index element for count entries. Removes the attribute entirely if all values are deleted.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.
attr must be a non-NULL pointer to an ipp_attribute_t* belonging to ipp (double pointer allows replacement or NULLing).
element must be a valid starting index within the attribute’s value count; count must not exceed the number of remaining values.
Callers must handle a potential change to *attr (e.g., it may become NULL if the attribute is removed).

functions.name: ippEnumString
functions.description: Returns the canonical keyword/name string for the specified enumeration value of the named attribute, if known.
requirements: attrname must be a non-NULL attribute name for an enumeration-valued attribute.
enumvalue should be a valid value for the named attribute (unknown values may return NULL or an implementation-defined string).

functions.name: ippEnumValue
functions.description: Returns the integer enumeration value corresponding to the given keyword/name string for the named attribute.
requirements: attrname must be a non-NULL enumeration attribute name.
enumstring must be a non-NULL canonical keyword/name for the enumeration.

functions.name: ippErrorString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for the given IPP status/error code.
requirements: error must be a valid ipp_status_t code; unknown codes may map to a generic or NULL string (implementation-defined).

functions.name: ippErrorValue
functions.description: Parses and returns an IPP status code from its keyword/name string.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL status keyword/name.

functions.name: ippFileClose
functions.description: Closes an IPP data file handle opened with ippFileOpen and releases resources.
requirements: file must be a valid ipp_file_t previously opened.
Do not use file after successful close.

functions.name: ippFileDelete
functions.description: Deletes an IPP data file object, closing it if necessary and freeing resources.
requirements: file must be a valid ipp_file_t* created by ippFileNew.
After deletion, file must not be used.

functions.name: ippFileExpandVars
functions.signature: size_t ippFileExpandVars(ipp_file_t *file, char *dst, const char *src, size_t dstsize);
functions.description: Expands variables in src using the file’s variable table into dst, returning the number of bytes that would be written.
requirements: file must be valid.
src must be a non-NULL source string.
If dst is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer of size at least dstsize bytes; ensure dstsize is sufficient for expansion.
Variable definitions must have been set using ippFileSetVar/ippFileSetVarf as needed.

functions.name: ippFileGetAttribute
functions.description: Gets a named attribute (and matching value tag) from the attribute set associated with the IPP data file parser.
requirements: file must be valid and must have attributes loaded/associated (e.g., via ippFileSetAttributes or reading).
name must be non-NULL; value_tag can be IPP_TAG_ZERO to ignore type filtering or a specific tag to match.

functions.name: ippFileGetAttributes
functions.description: Returns the IPP attribute set (as an ipp_t collection) currently associated with the IPP data file parser.
requirements: file must be valid and have attributes associated.

functions.name: ippFileGetFilename
functions.description: Returns the filename currently associated with the IPP data file, if any.
requirements: file must be valid.

functions.name: ippFileGetLineNumber
functions.description: Returns the current parser line number for the IPP data file.
requirements: file must be valid.

functions.name: ippFileGetVar
functions.description: Gets the value of a named variable from the IPP data file parser’s variable table.
requirements: file must be valid.
name must be non-NULL.
