functions.name: ippFileNew
functions.signature: ipp_file_t *ippFileNew(ipp_file_t *parent, ipp_fattr_cb_t attr_cb, ipp_ferror_cb_t error_cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Creates a new IPP data file parser object, optionally inheriting settings from a parent and setting callbacks for attribute and error handling.
requirements: parent may be NULL or a valid ipp_file_t to inherit from.
attr_cb and error_cb may be NULL or valid function pointers; cb_data is passed to callbacks.
Caller must later close/delete the object with ippFileClose/ippFileDelete.

functions.name: ippFileOpen
functions.signature: bool ippFileOpen(ipp_file_t *file, const char *filename, const char *mode);
functions.description: Opens a file for reading/writing IPP attribute files using the parser.
requirements: file must be a valid ipp_file_t created by ippFileNew.
filename must be non-NULL and refer to an accessible file path.
mode must be a valid fopen-style mode string (e.g., "r", "w").

functions.name: ippFileRead
functions.signature: bool ippFileRead(ipp_file_t *file, ipp_ftoken_cb_t token_cb, bool with_groups);
functions.description: Reads and tokenizes/parses the opened IPP attribute file, optionally reporting tokens via callback and grouping attributes by group tags.
requirements: file must be open with ippFileOpen.
token_cb may be NULL (no token callback) or a valid function pointer; with_groups selects whether group tags are included/expected.

functions.name: ippFileReadCollection
functions.description: Reads a collection value from the current position in the IPP attribute file, returning it as an ipp_t (collection).
requirements: file must be valid and positioned at a collection in the input stream.
The returned collection must be freed by the caller via ippDelete when no longer needed.

functions.name: ippFileReadToken
functions.description: Reads the next token from the IPP attribute file into token buffer.
requirements: file must be valid and open.
token must be non-NULL and point to a buffer of size tokensize > 0.

functions.name: ippFileRestorePosition
functions.description: Restores the last position previously saved in the IPP data file parser.
requirements: file must be valid.
A position must have been saved earlier via ippFileSavePosition.

functions.name: ippFileSavePosition
functions.description: Saves the current position in the IPP data file parser for later restoration.
requirements: file must be valid.

functions.name: ippFileSetAttributes
functions.description: Associates a set of attributes (as an ipp_t) with the IPP data file parser.
requirements: file must be valid.
attrs must be a valid ipp_t pointer (typically a collection used as an attribute set).

functions.name: ippFileSetGroupTag
functions.description: Sets the current group tag used when writing attributes via the IPP data file parser.
requirements: file must be valid.
group_tag must be a valid group tag (e.g., IPP_TAG_OPERATION, IPP_TAG_PRINTER, etc.).

functions.name: ippFileSetVar
functions.signature: bool ippFileSetVar(ipp_file_t *file, const char *name, const char *value);
functions.description: Defines or updates a variable in the IPP data file parser’s variable table.
requirements: file must be valid.
name and value must be non-NULL strings.

functions.name: ippFileSetVarf
functions.signature: bool ippFileSetVarf(ipp_file_t *file, const char *name, const char *value, ...);
functions.description: Defines/updates a variable using printf-style formatting of the value in the parser’s variable table.
requirements: file must be valid.
name must be non-NULL.
value is a printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format.

functions.name: ippFileWriteAttributes
functions.description: Writes attributes from an IPP message to the IPP attribute file in a textual form, optionally including group tags.
requirements: file must be valid and open for writing.
ipp must be a valid IPP message containing attributes to write.

functions.name: ippFileWriteComment
functions.description: Writes a formatted comment line to the IPP attribute file.
requirements: file must be valid and open for writing.
comment must be a non-NULL printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format.

functions.name: ippFileWriteToken
functions.description: Writes a single token to the IPP attribute file.
requirements: file must be valid and open for writing.
token must be a non-NULL string.

functions.name: ippFileWriteTokenf
functions.description: Writes a formatted token to the IPP attribute file.
requirements: file must be valid and open for writing.
token must be a non-NULL printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format.

functions.name: ippFindAttribute
functions.description: Finds the first attribute with the specified name (and optionally matching value tag) in the IPP message, starting from the beginning.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.
name must be non-NULL; value_tag may be IPP_TAG_ZERO to ignore type filtering or a specific tag to require type match.

functions.name: ippFindNextAttribute
functions.description: Continues searching for the next occurrence of an attribute with the given name (and optionally matching value tag) from the current iterator position.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message and iteration state must be positioned by a prior call to ippFindAttribute/ippFindNextAttribute.
name must be non-NULL; value_tag may filter matches.

functions.name: ippGetBoolean
functions.description: Returns the boolean value at the given element index of a boolean attribute.
requirements: attr must be a valid attribute of boolean type.
element must be less than the attribute’s value count.

functions.name: ippGetCollection
functions.description: Returns the collection (as ipp_t*) at the given element index of a collection-valued attribute.
requirements: attr must be a valid attribute of collection type.
element must be less than the attribute’s value count.
The returned ipp_t* is owned by the attribute; do not free it directly.

functions.name: ippGetCount
functions.description: Returns the number of values in the given attribute (1 for single-valued, N for multi-valued).
requirements: attr must be a valid attribute pointer.

functions.name: ippGetDate
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the date/time value at the given element index of a date attribute.
requirements: attr must be a valid date/time attribute.
element must be less than the attribute’s value count.
Returned pointer is to internal storage; do not modify or free.

functions.name: ippGetFirstAttribute
functions.description: Returns the first attribute in the IPP message and initializes internal iteration state.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.

functions.name: ippGetGroupTag
functions.description: Returns the group tag (e.g., operation, job, printer) associated with the given attribute.
requirements: attr must be a valid attribute pointer.

functions.name: ippGetInteger
functions.description: Returns the integer/enum value at the given element index of an integer/enum attribute.
requirements: attr must be a valid integer/enum attribute.
element must be less than the attribute’s value count.

functions.name: ippGetLength
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of the IPP message when encoded (or the current data length), useful for I/O operations.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.

functions.name: ippGetName
functions.description: Returns the attribute’s name string.
requirements: attr must be a valid attribute pointer.
Returned pointer is owned by the attribute; do not modify or free.

functions.name: ippGetNextAttribute
functions.description: Returns the next attribute in the IPP message based on the current iterator position.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message and iteration state must be initialized via ippGetFirstAttribute or prior call to ippGetNextAttribute.

functions.name: ippGetOctetString
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the octet string (byte array) at the specified element index and optionally its length via datalen.
requirements: attr must be a valid octetString attribute.
element must be less than the attribute’s value count.
If datalen is non-NULL, it will receive the number of bytes in the value.
Returned pointer is to internal storage; do not modify or free.

functions.name: ippGetOperation
functions.description: Returns the operation code for a request message.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message representing a request.

functions.name: ippGetPort
functions.description: Returns the TCP port number currently used for IPP (default typically 631).

functions.name: ippGetRange
functions.description: Returns the lower bound of the range value at element index for a rangeOfInteger attribute and, if upper is non-NULL, stores the upper bound.
requirements: attr must be a valid rangeOfInteger attribute.
element must be less than the attribute’s value count.
If upper is non-NULL, it must point to writable memory for the upper bound.

functions.name: ippGetRequestId
functions.description: Returns the request-id value of the IPP message.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.

functions.name: ippGetResolution
functions.signature: int ippGetResolution(ipp_attribute_t *attr, size_t element, int *yres, ipp_res_t *units);
functions.description: Returns the X resolution of the resolution value at the given index and optionally returns the Y resolution and units.
requirements: attr must be a valid resolution attribute.
element must be less than the attribute’s value count.
If yres is non-NULL, it must point to writable memory; if units is non-NULL, it must point to writable memory.

functions.name: ippGetState
functions.description: Returns the current state of the IPP message object (e.g., idle, header, attribute, data, or error).
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.

functions.name: ippGetStatusCode
functions.description: Returns the status-code for a response message.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message representing a response.

functions.name: ippGetString
functions.signature: const char *ippGetString(ipp_attribute_t *attr, size_t element, const char **language);
functions.description: Returns the string value at the given element index of a string-valued attribute and optionally its language (for text/name-with-language types).
requirements: attr must be a valid string-compatible attribute.
element must be less than the attribute’s value count.
If language is non-NULL, it receives a pointer to the language tag (may be NULL if not applicable).
Returned string pointer is to internal storage; do not modify or free.

functions.name: ippGetValueTag
functions.description: Returns the value tag (type) of the given attribute (e.g., integer, boolean, keyword, text, range, etc.).
requirements: attr must be a valid attribute pointer.

functions.name: ippGetVersion
functions.description: Returns the major version of the IPP message and optionally stores the minor version through the minor pointer.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.
If minor is non-NULL, it must point to writable memory.

functions.name: ippNew
functions.description: Creates a new, empty IPP message object.
requirements: Caller must delete the returned object with ippDelete when done.

functions.name: ippNewRequest
functions.description: Creates a new IPP request message initialized with the given operation code.
requirements: op must be a valid IPP operation.
Caller must delete the returned object with ippDelete.

functions.name: ippNewResponse
functions.description: Creates a new IPP response message using the supplied request as a template (e.g., copies version and request-id).
requirements: request must be a valid IPP request object.
Caller must delete the returned object with ippDelete.

functions.name: ippOpString
functions.description: Returns the keyword/name string for the given IPP operation code.
requirements: op should be a valid ipp_op_t; unknown values may return a generic or NULL string.

functions.name: ippOpValue
functions.description: Returns the IPP operation code parsed from the keyword/name string.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL operation keyword/name string.

functions.name: ippRead
functions.description: Reads/decodes an IPP message from the given HTTP connection into the ipp object, advancing the message state.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t* connection (from CUPS HTTP API).
ipp must be a valid IPP message object in a state ready to receive data.

functions.name: ippReadFile
functions.description: Reads/decodes an IPP message from a file descriptor into the ipp object.
requirements: fd must be a valid readable file descriptor positioned at the start of an IPP message.
ipp must be a valid IPP message object ready to receive data.

functions.name: ippReadIO
functions.signature: ipp_state_t ippReadIO(void *src, ipp_io_cb_t cb, bool blocking, ipp_t *parent, ipp_t *ipp);
functions.description: Reads/decodes an IPP message from an arbitrary I/O source using a callback to supply bytes.
requirements: cb must be a valid callback of type ipp_io_cb_t that reads up to 'bytes' into 'buffer' and returns the number of bytes read or -1 on error.
src is an opaque pointer passed to the callback (must be valid for cb).
blocking selects whether the read should block for data.
parent may be NULL or a related IPP object for context; ipp must be a valid target message.

functions.name: ippRestore
functions.description: Restores a previously saved iterator/state for the IPP message (inverse of ippSave).
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.
ippSave must have been called earlier to establish a saved state.

functions.name: ippSave
functions.description: Saves the current iterator/state of the IPP message so it can be restored later with ippRestore.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.

functions.name: ippSetBoolean
functions.signature: bool ippSetBoolean(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, size_t element, bool boolvalue);
functions.description: Sets or replaces the boolean value at the specified element index of an existing boolean attribute, possibly creating it if attr refers to a new slot.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.
attr must be a non-NULL pointer to an attribute pointer that refers to a boolean attribute within ipp or a location to create/update.
element must be within allowable range for the attribute (existing count or next index if growing, per implementation).

functions.name: ippSetCollection
functions.signature: bool ippSetCollection(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, size_t element, ipp_t *colvalue);
functions.description: Sets or replaces the collection value at the specified element index of a collection attribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must be a pointer to an attribute pointer for a collection-valued attribute in ipp.
element must be within the attribute’s allowable range.
colvalue must be a valid ipp_t* representing a collection.

functions.name: ippSetDate
functions.signature: bool ippSetDate(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, size_t element, const ipp_uchar_t *datevalue);
functions.description: Sets/replaces the date value at the specified element index of a date attribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a date attribute in ipp (via pointer to attribute pointer).
element must be within the attribute’s allowable range.
datevalue must point to a valid IPP date/time encoding.

functions.name: ippSetGroupTag
functions.description: Changes the group tag of an attribute within the IPP message.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference an existing attribute in ipp (pointer to attribute pointer).
group_tag must be a valid group tag.

functions.name: ippSetInteger
functions.signature: bool ippSetInteger(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, size_t element, int intvalue);
functions.description: Sets/replaces the integer/enum value at the given element index of an integer/enum attribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference an integer/enum attribute in ipp (pointer to attribute pointer).
element must be within the attribute’s allowable range.

functions.name: ippSetName
functions.description: Renames an existing attribute to the provided name.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference an existing attribute in ipp.
name must be non-NULL and a valid IPP attribute name.

functions.name: ippSetOctetString
functions.signature: bool ippSetOctetString(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, size_t element, const void *data, size_t datalen);
functions.description: Sets/replaces the octetString value at the given element index of an octetString attribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference an octetString attribute in ipp (pointer to attribute pointer).
element must be within the attribute’s allowable range.
If datalen > 0, data must be non-NULL; datalen should not exceed IPP_MAX_OCTETSTRING for a single value.

functions.name: ippSetOperation
functions.description: Sets the operation code of the IPP request message.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.
op must be a valid IPP operation code.

functions.name: ippSetPort
functions.description: Sets the TCP port number used for IPP connections globally.
requirements: p should be a valid TCP port number in the range 1–65535.

functions.name: ippSetRange
functions.signature: bool ippSetRange(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, size_t element, int lowervalue, int uppervalue);
functions.description: Sets/replaces the range value at the specified element index of a rangeOfInteger attribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a rangeOfInteger attribute in ipp.
element must be within the attribute’s allowable range.
lowervalue and uppervalue should define a valid inclusive range (typically lowervalue <= uppervalue).

functions.name: ippSetRequestId
functions.description: Sets the request-id of the IPP message.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
request_id should be a positive integer within the valid range for IPP request IDs.

functions.name: ippSetResolution
functions.signature: bool ippSetResolution(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, size_t element, ipp_res_t unitsvalue, int xresvalue, int yresvalue);
functions.description: Sets/replaces the resolution value at the specified element index of a resolution attribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a resolution attribute in ipp.
element must be within the attribute’s allowable range.
unitsvalue must be a valid ipp_res_t; xresvalue and yresvalue must be positive integers.

functions.name: ippSetState
functions.description: Sets the state of the IPP message object (used internally to control reading/writing/encoding).
requirements: ipp must be valid.
state must be a valid ipp_state_t value.

functions.name: ippSetStatusCode
functions.description: Sets the status-code for an IPP response message.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message representing a response.
status must be a valid ipp_status_t.

functions.name: ippSetString
functions.signature: bool ippSetString(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, size_t element, const char *strvalue);
functions.description: Sets/replaces the string value at the specified element index of a string-valued attribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a string-compatible attribute in ipp.
element must be within the attribute’s allowable range.
strvalue must be a non-NULL string that satisfies the constraints of the attribute’s value tag (length/characters).

functions.name: ippSetStringf
functions.signature: bool ippSetStringf(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, size_t element, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Sets/replaces the string value using printf-style formatting at the given element index of a string-valued attribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a string-compatible attribute in ipp.
element must be within the attribute’s allowable range.
format must be a non-NULL printf-style format string with matching arguments.
Result must satisfy the attribute’s constraints (length/characters).

functions.name: ippSetStringfv
functions.signature: bool ippSetStringfv(ipp_t *ipp, ipp_attribute_t **attr, size_t element, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: Sets/replaces the string value using a va_list at the specified element index of a string-valued attribute.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference a string-compatible attribute in ipp.
element must be within the attribute’s allowable range.
format must be non-NULL; ap must be a valid va_list matching the format.
Result must satisfy the attribute’s constraints.

functions.name: ippSetValueTag
functions.description: Changes the value tag (type) of an attribute (e.g., from keyword to name) while keeping its values, as allowed.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
attr must reference an existing attribute in ipp.
value_tag must be a valid value tag appropriate for the attribute’s contents (caller must ensure compatibility).

functions.name: ippSetVersion
functions.signature: bool ippSetVersion(ipp_t *ipp, int major, int minor);
functions.description: Sets the IPP protocol version (major.minor) for the message.
requirements: ipp must be valid.
major and minor should be valid protocol version numbers (e.g., 2.0, 2.1).

functions.name: ippStateString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for the given IPP message state.
requirements: state must be a valid ipp_state_t value.

functions.name: ippTagString
functions.description: Returns the human-readable name for the given IPP tag (value or group).
requirements: tag must be a valid ipp_tag_t value; unknown values may map to a generic string or NULL.

functions.name: ippTagValue
functions.description: Parses and returns the IPP tag value corresponding to the provided tag name string.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL tag name string.

functions.name: ippTimeToDate
functions.description: Converts a time_t to an IPP date/time byte array (IPP_TAG_DATE encoding) and returns a pointer to it.
requirements: t is a time value to convert.
Returned pointer refers to memory managed by the library; treat as read-only and copy if longer-lived storage is needed.

functions.name: ippValidateAttribute
functions.description: Validates that an attribute’s name, value tag, and values conform to IPP syntax/rules.
requirements: attr must be a valid attribute pointer.

functions.name: ippValidateAttributes
functions.description: Validates that all attributes in the IPP message conform to IPP syntax/rules and that the message is well-formed.
requirements: ipp must be a valid IPP message.

functions.name: ippWrite
functions.description: Encodes/writes an IPP message to the given HTTP connection, advancing the message’s I/O state.
requirements: http must be a valid http_t* connection ready for writing.
ipp must be a valid IPP message prepared for sending (e.g., correct operation, attributes set).

functions.name: ippWriteFile
functions.description: Encodes/writes an IPP message to the given file descriptor.
requirements: fd must be a valid writable file descriptor.
ipp must be a valid IPP message prepared for sending.

functions.name: ippWriteIO
functions.signature: ipp_state_t ippWriteIO(void *dst, ipp_io_cb_t cb, bool blocking, ipp_t *parent, ipp_t *ipp);
functions.description: Encodes/writes an IPP message to an arbitrary destination using a callback to consume bytes.
requirements: cb must be a valid ipp_io_cb_t that writes up to 'bytes' from 'buffer' and returns the number of bytes written or -1 on error.
dst is an opaque pointer provided to the callback and must be valid for cb.
blocking selects whether the write should block.
parent may be NULL or a related IPP object for context; ipp must be a valid message to write.

functions.name: httpAcceptConnection
functions.description: Accepts an incoming TCP connection on the listening socket fd and returns a new HTTP connection object. Use when implementing an HTTP server that has already accepted/obtained a socket. The blocking flag sets the connection’s blocking mode.
requirements: fd must be a valid connected socket descriptor for an accepted client connection
blocking selects blocking (true) or non-blocking (false) I/O on the returned connection
Caller must close the returned http_t* with httpClose when done
On failure, returns NULL; caller must handle NULL

functions.name: httpAddrClose
functions.description: Closes a socket associated with the given address. Primarily a helper to close fd with any platform-specific handling related to addr.
requirements: addr may be used for platform-specific close semantics; pass the same addr used to open/listen/connect when available
fd must be a valid open socket descriptor
Returns true on success, false on failure; caller should check return value

functions.name: httpAddrConnect
functions.description: Attempts to connect to one of the addresses in addrlist, returning the address that succeeded and the connected socket through sock. Honors a timeout and optional cancellation.
requirements: addrlist must be a valid list created by httpAddrGetList or httpAddrCopyList
sock must be non-NULL and will receive the connected socket descriptor on success
msec should be >= 0 to set a timeout in milliseconds; 0 may mean no wait or immediate depending on implementation
cancel may be NULL; if non-NULL, non-zero value aborts the attempt
Returns NULL on failure (no address connected or cancelled); caller must check and avoid using sock unless function succeeds

functions.name: httpAddrCopyList
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of the provided address list.
requirements: src must be NULL or a valid address list
Returned list must be freed with httpAddrFreeList
Returns NULL on allocation failure

functions.name: httpAddrFreeList
functions.description: Frees an address list previously created by httpAddrGetList or httpAddrCopyList.
requirements: addrlist may be NULL (no-op) or a list allocated by this API
After calling, addrlist must not be used

functions.name: httpAddrGetFamily
functions.description: Returns the socket family (e.g., AF_INET, AF_INET6, AF_LOCAL) for the given address.
requirements: addr must be a valid pointer to an initialized http_addr_t

functions.name: httpAddrGetLength
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of the underlying sockaddr for addr, suitable for system calls.
requirements: addr must be a valid pointer to an initialized http_addr_t

functions.name: httpAddrGetList
functions.signature: http_addrlist_t *httpAddrGetList(const char *hostname, int family, const char *service);
functions.description: Resolves hostname and service to a list of socket addresses, optionally constrained to a specific address family.
requirements: hostname must be a valid host or address string
family should be AF_UNSPEC, AF_INET, AF_INET6, or AF_LOCAL as supported
service may be a service name or numeric string; may be NULL to use defaults
Returns NULL on resolution failure; caller must check and free result with httpAddrFreeList when done

functions.name: httpAddrGetPort
functions.description: Gets the TCP/UDP port number stored in the address, in host byte order.
requirements: addr must be a valid pointer to a socket address with a port field

functions.name: httpAddrGetString
functions.description: Converts addr to a human-readable string (numeric address) and writes it into s.
requirements: addr must be valid and initialized
s must be a non-NULL writable buffer
slen must be the size of s in bytes and large enough to hold the address string and terminator
Returns s on success or NULL on failure; caller must check

functions.name: httpAddrIsAny
functions.description: Returns whether addr represents a wildcard/any-address (e.g., 0.0.0.0 or ::).
requirements: addr must be a valid initialized address

functions.name: httpAddrIsEqual
functions.description: Compares two socket addresses (http_addr_t) for equality and returns true if they refer to the same address, otherwise false. Typical usage: supply two initialized addresses (IPv4/IPv6/UNIX-domain) you want to test for equivalence. Whether the comparison includes the port/service component or only the host/address portion is not documented here and is therefore unknown; treat the result as an address-level equality check unless you confirm otherwise from implementation or external docs.
requirements: addr1 must point to a valid, initialized http_addr_t.
addr2 must point to a valid, initialized http_addr_t.
Input addresses should represent meaningful/fully-populated socket addresses (family set and address bytes set) for a deterministic comparison.
Addresses should be of the same address family for a meaningful comparison; behavior regarding cross-family comparison is not documented here.
Return value must be checked: true indicates equality, false indicates inequality.

functions.name: httpAddrIsLocalhost
functions.description: Returns whether addr refers to the local host (e.g., 127.0.0.1, ::1, or a local domain socket).
requirements: addr must be a valid initialized address

functions.name: httpAddrListen
functions.description: Creates a listening socket bound to addr and port and returns the socket descriptor.
requirements: addr must be a valid local address to bind
port must be in the valid TCP port range (0–65535); 0 may request an ephemeral port
Returns -1 on failure; caller must check and close the socket on success when finished

functions.name: httpAddrLookup
functions.description: Performs a reverse lookup of addr to a hostname and writes it into name.
requirements: addr must be valid and initialized
name must be a non-NULL writable buffer
namelen must be the size of name in bytes; must be sufficient to hold the hostname and terminator
Returns name on success or NULL on failure

functions.name: httpAddrSetPort
functions.description: Sets the port number in the given address to port (host byte order).
requirements: addr must be valid and point to a sockaddr that has a port
port must be in range 0–65535

functions.name: httpAssembleURI
functions.signature: http_uri_status_t httpAssembleURI(http_uri_coding_t encoding, char *uri, size_t urilen, const char *scheme, const char *username, const char *host, int port, const char *resource);
functions.description: Builds a URI string from its components using the specified encoding rules and writes it into uri.
requirements: uri must be a non-NULL writable buffer
urilen must be the size of uri; must be large enough for the result including terminator
encoding controls percent-encoding; choose appropriate flags
scheme, host, resource may be NULL depending on desired output; invalid combinations may yield error statuses
Returns a http_uri_status_t indicating success or the reason for failure/overflow; caller must check

functions.name: httpAssembleURIf
functions.signature: http_uri_status_t httpAssembleURIf(http_uri_coding_t encoding, char *uri, size_t urilen, const char *scheme, const char *username, const char *host, int port, const char *resourcef, ...);
functions.description: Builds a URI string like httpAssembleURI but formats the resource path using printf-like formatting and varargs.
requirements: uri must be a non-NULL writable buffer
urilen must be sufficient for the formatted result including terminator
resourcef must be a valid printf-style format string for the resource component; varargs must match the format
Returns a http_uri_status_t; caller must check for OVERFLOW and BAD_* errors

functions.name: httpAssembleUUID
functions.signature: char *httpAssembleUUID(const char *server, int port, const char *name, int number, char *buffer, size_t bufsize);
functions.description: Constructs a stable UUID string for a CUPS object based on server, port, name, and number, writing it to buffer.
requirements: buffer must be non-NULL and writable
bufsize must be large enough to hold the UUID string (recommend >= 128)
server and name should be non-NULL strings; semantics if NULL are implementation-defined
Returns buffer on success or NULL on failure

functions.name: httpClearFields
functions.description: Clears any set/request/response header fields associated with the HTTP connection.
requirements: http must be a valid connection pointer
Call before composing a new request or response if you need a clean set of fields

functions.name: httpClose
functions.description: Closes and frees an HTTP connection, releasing any associated resources.
requirements: http may be NULL (no-op) or a valid connection returned by httpConnect/httpAcceptConnection
After calling, the http pointer must not be used

functions.name: httpClearCookie
functions.description: Clears any cookie value stored in the HTTP connection object.
requirements: http must be a valid connection pointer

functions.name: httpConnect
functions.signature: http_t *httpConnect(const char *host, int port, http_addrlist_t *addrlist, int family, http_encryption_t encryption, bool blocking, int msec, int *cancel);
functions.description: Establishes a client HTTP connection to host:port, optionally using a pre-resolved addrlist, address family preference, encryption policy, blocking mode, timeout, and cancel flag.
requirements: host must be a valid hostname or address; may be ignored if addrlist is provided
port must be 0–65535 (0 may imply default based on scheme)
addrlist may be NULL or from httpAddrGetList
family should be AF_UNSPEC/AF_INET/AF_INET6 as supported
encryption controls TLS usage per http_encryption_t
blocking selects blocking/non-blocking I/O
msec should be >= 0 for timeout
cancel may be NULL; if non-NULL, non-zero cancels the attempt
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check and later close with httpClose on success

functions.name: httpConnectAgain
functions.description: Attempts to reconnect an existing HTTP connection using its stored parameters, honoring a timeout and optional cancel.
requirements: http must be a valid connection pointer
msec should be >= 0 for timeout
cancel may be NULL; if non-NULL, non-zero cancels
Returns true on success, false on failure; caller must handle failure

functions.name: httpConnectURI
functions.signature: http_t *httpConnectURI(const char *uri, char *host, size_t hsize, int *port, char *resource, size_t rsize, bool blocking, int msec, int *cancel, bool require_ca);
functions.description: Parses the given URI and connects to the indicated HTTP/HTTPS endpoint. Optionally returns parsed host, port, and resource to the provided buffers.
requirements: uri must be a valid URI string
host may be NULL or a writable buffer with size hsize for the hostname
port may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive the port
resource may be NULL or a writable buffer with size rsize for the resource path
blocking selects blocking/non-blocking I/O
msec should be >= 0 for timeout
cancel may be NULL; if non-NULL, non-zero cancels
require_ca controls certificate requirements for TLS; exact behavior not documented here
Returns NULL on failure; close with httpClose on success

functions.name: httpCopyPeerCredentials
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated string describing or containing peer credentials for the connection (e.g., user or cert info).
requirements: http must be a valid connection pointer
Returned string must be freed by the caller
Returns NULL on failure or when not available

functions.name: httpDecode64
functions.signature: char *httpDecode64(char *out, size_t *outlen, const char *in, const char **end);
functions.description: Decodes Base64 (or URL-safe?) input from in into binary data in out. Writes the number of bytes decoded to outlen and optionally returns the position of the first non-decoded character in end.
requirements: out must be a writable buffer large enough to hold the decoded data
outlen must be non-NULL; on input may indicate capacity or may be output-only (unspecified), on output receives decoded length
in must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string of Base64 data
end may be NULL or will receive a pointer into in after the last processed character
Returns out on success or NULL on error; caller must check

functions.name: httpEncode64
functions.signature: char *httpEncode64(char *out, size_t outlen, const char *in, size_t inlen, bool url);
functions.description: Encodes binary input in into Base64 and writes to out. If url is true, uses URL-safe Base64 alphabet.
requirements: out must be a writable buffer
outlen must be large enough to hold the encoded output including terminator
in must point to inlen bytes of input; may be binary
Returns out on success or NULL on failure

functions.name: httpFieldValue
functions.description: Maps an HTTP header field name string to the corresponding http_field_t enum value.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL header field name
Unknown names return HTTP_FIELD_UNKNOWN; caller must handle

functions.name: httpFlush
functions.description: Flushes any pending read data and/or resets the read state on the HTTP connection. Intended to discard buffered input.
requirements: http must be a valid connection pointer

functions.name: httpFlushWrite
functions.description: Flushes any buffered write data on the HTTP connection to the socket.
requirements: http must be a valid connection pointer
Returns 0 or positive on success and -1 on error (exact convention not documented); caller must check

functions.name: httpGetActivity
functions.description: Returns the time of last activity on the connection (read or write).
requirements: http must be a valid connection pointer

functions.name: httpGetAddress
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the peer address structure for the connection.
requirements: http must be a valid connection pointer
Returned pointer remains owned by the connection; do not free or modify beyond documented helpers

functions.name: httpGetAuthString
functions.description: Returns the current Authorization header value string for the connection, if any.
requirements: http must be valid
Returned pointer is managed by the connection and remains valid until modified; do not free

functions.name: httpGetBlocking
functions.description: Returns whether the connection is in blocking I/O mode.
requirements: http must be valid

functions.name: httpGetContentEncoding
functions.description: Returns the Content-Encoding value for the current message, if any.
requirements: http must be valid
Returned pointer is owned by the connection; do not free

functions.name: httpGetCookie
functions.description: Returns the current Cookie header value stored on the connection, if any.
requirements: http must be valid
Returned pointer is owned by the connection; do not free

functions.name: httpGetCookieValue
functions.signature: char *httpGetCookieValue(http_t *http, const char *name, char *buffer, size_t bufsize);
functions.description: Looks up a cookie by name from the connection’s stored cookies and writes the value into buffer.
requirements: http must be valid
name must be a non-NULL cookie name
buffer must be a writable buffer of size bufsize
Returns buffer on success or NULL if not found or on error

functions.name: httpGetDateString
functions.signature: const char *httpGetDateString(time_t t, char *s, size_t slen);
functions.description: Formats the given time value t into an RFC 7231 HTTP-date string in buffer s.
requirements: s must be a writable buffer
slen must be large enough to hold the formatted date and terminator (recommend >= 32)
Returns s on success or NULL on failure

functions.name: httpGetDateTime
functions.description: Parses an HTTP-date string s and returns the corresponding time value.
requirements: s must point to a valid HTTP date/time string
On parse failure, returns 0 or (time_t)-1 depending on implementation; caller must detect invalid input

functions.name: httpGetEncryption
functions.description: Returns the current encryption/TLS policy/state for the connection.
requirements: http must be valid

functions.name: httpGetError
functions.description: Returns the last error code associated with the connection/socket.
requirements: http must be valid
Error code semantics follow platform errno/socket error conventions

functions.name: httpGetExpect
functions.description: Returns the current Expect status/value for the connection’s pending request (e.g., 100-continue).
requirements: http must be valid

functions.name: httpGetFd
functions.description: Returns the underlying socket file descriptor for the connection.
requirements: http must be valid
Descriptor is managed by the connection; do not close directly unless documented

functions.name: httpGetField
functions.description: Returns the value string of the specified header field for the current message on the connection.
requirements: http must be valid
field must be a valid http_field_t
Returned pointer is owned by the connection; do not free

functions.name: httpGetHostname
functions.description: Returns the local or peer hostname associated with the connection, optionally writing it into s.
requirements: http must be valid
s may be NULL or a writable buffer of size slen
Returned pointer is a string that may be s or an internal buffer; do not free

functions.name: httpGetKeepAlive
functions.description: Returns the keep-alive setting for the connection.
requirements: http must be valid

functions.name: httpGetLength
functions.description: Returns the expected content length for the current message body, if known.
requirements: http must be valid

functions.name: httpGetPending
functions.description: Returns the number of input bytes currently buffered and pending to be read from the connection.
requirements: http must be valid

functions.name: httpGetReady
functions.description: Returns the number of output bytes that can be written without blocking, or amount ready (implementation-defined).
requirements: http must be valid
Caller must treat 0 carefully with non-blocking I/O

functions.name: httpGetRemaining
functions.description: Returns the remaining number of bytes expected for the current message body (if known).
requirements: http must be valid

functions.name: httpGetSecurity
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description of the connection security (e.g., TLS version/cipher), optionally writing into buffer.
requirements: http must be valid
buffer may be NULL or a writable buffer of size bufsize
Returned pointer may be buffer or an internal string; do not free

functions.name: httpGetState
functions.description: Returns the current HTTP state of the connection (request/response lifecycle).
requirements: http must be valid

functions.name: httpGetStatus
functions.description: Returns the current HTTP status code associated with the last operation or response.
requirements: http must be valid

functions.name: httpGetSubField
functions.signature: char *httpGetSubField(http_t *http, http_field_t field, const char *name, char *value, size_t valuelen);
functions.description: Parses a structured header field and extracts the value of the named parameter into value.
requirements: http must be valid
field must be a valid http_field_t
name must be a non-NULL parameter name
value must be a writable buffer of size valuelen
Returns value on success or NULL if not present or on error

functions.name: httpGetVersion
functions.description: Returns the HTTP protocol version negotiated/used on the connection.
requirements: http must be valid

functions.name: httpGets
functions.description: Reads a CRLF-terminated line from the connection into line up to length-1 chars and NUL-terminates it.
requirements: http must be valid
line must be a writable buffer
length must be > 0 and is the size of line
Returns line on success or NULL on EOF/error

functions.name: httpInitialize
functions.description: Initializes global HTTP/CUPS networking state for the process. Typically optional as initialization is automatic on first use.
requirements: Must be called before using APIs only if explicit early initialization is needed
Safe to call multiple times (expected)

functions.name: httpIsChunked
functions.description: Returns whether the current message uses chunked transfer encoding.
requirements: http must be valid

functions.name: httpIsEncrypted
functions.description: Returns whether the connection is currently using TLS encryption.
requirements: http must be valid

functions.name: httpPeek
functions.description: Peeks at incoming data without consuming it, copying up to length bytes into buffer.
requirements: http must be valid
buffer must be writable and at least length bytes
Returns number of bytes peeked or -1 on error; 0 may indicate no data

functions.name: httpPrintf
functions.description: Formats and writes text to the connection using printf-style formatting.
requirements: http must be valid
format must be a valid printf-style format string; varargs must match
Returns number of bytes written, or -1 on error

functions.name: httpRead
functions.description: Reads up to length bytes from the connection into buffer, following HTTP message framing.
requirements: http must be valid
buffer must be writable and at least length bytes
Returns number of bytes read, 0 on EOF, or -1 on error

functions.name: httpReadRequest
functions.description: Reads and parses an HTTP request line and headers from the connection, writing the request-target/resource into resource.
requirements: http must be valid
resource must be a writable buffer of size resourcelen
Returns a http_state_t indicating the parsed method/state or an error state; caller must check

functions.name: httpResolveHostname
functions.description: Resolves and returns the canonical hostname for the connection’s peer, optionally writing it into buffer.
requirements: http must be valid
buffer may be NULL or a writable buffer of size bufsize
Returned pointer may be buffer or an internal string; do not free

functions.name: httpResolveURI
functions.signature: const char *httpResolveURI(const char *uri, char *resolved_uri, size_t resolved_size, http_resolve_t options, http_resolve_cb_t cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Resolves a CUPS/IPP-related URI into a canonical/usable form based on options and an optional callback, writing it into resolved_uri and returning it.
requirements: uri must be a valid URI string
resolved_uri must be a writable buffer of size resolved_size
options is a bitfield of http_resolve_t flags controlling resolution behavior
cb may be NULL or a callback to be invoked during resolution; cb_data is passed to cb
Returns resolved_uri on success or NULL on failure

functions.name: httpSeparateURI
functions.signature: http_uri_status_t httpSeparateURI(http_uri_coding_t decoding, const char *uri, char *scheme, size_t schemelen, char *username, size_t usernamelen, char *host, size_t hostlen, int *port, char *resource, size_t resourcelen);
functions.description: Parses URI into its components, applying the specified decoding rules, and writes components into the provided buffers and port integer.
requirements: uri must be a valid URI string
Each component buffer may be NULL if not needed; when non-NULL the corresponding length must be the buffer size
port may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive the port
Returns a http_uri_status_t indicating success or a specific parse error; caller must check

functions.name: httpSetAuthString
functions.signature: void httpSetAuthString(http_t *http, const char *scheme, const char *data);
functions.description: Sets the Authorization header for subsequent requests on the connection using the given scheme and data.
requirements: http must be valid
scheme must be a valid auth scheme (e.g., "Basic", "Bearer"); data must be appropriate for the scheme
Overwrites any existing Authorization value

functions.name: httpSetBlocking
functions.description: Sets the connection’s blocking I/O mode to b.
requirements: http must be valid
Changing to non-blocking may affect subsequent read/write return values

functions.name: httpSetCookie
functions.description: Sets the Cookie header value for subsequent requests on the connection.
requirements: http must be valid
cookie may be NULL to clear or a valid cookie string

functions.name: httpSetDefaultField
functions.signature: void httpSetDefaultField(http_t *http, http_field_t field, const char *value);
functions.description: Sets a default header field value that will be used if not otherwise specified when sending requests.
requirements: http must be valid
field must be a valid http_field_t
value may be NULL to clear or a header value string

functions.name: httpSetEncryption
functions.description: Configures the encryption/TLS policy for the connection, potentially initiating or shutting down TLS.
requirements: http must be valid
e must be a valid http_encryption_t value
May fail depending on server support or certificate validation; returns false on failure; caller must check

functions.name: httpSetExpect
functions.description: Sets the desired Expect behavior/status for subsequent requests (e.g., HTTP_STATUS_CONTINUE for 100-continue).
requirements: http must be valid
expect should be a relevant status code for Expect handling

functions.name: httpSetField
functions.signature: void httpSetField(http_t *http, http_field_t field, const char *value);
functions.description: Sets the value of a specific header field for the current/pending request.
requirements: http must be valid
field must be a valid http_field_t
value may be NULL to clear or a header value string

functions.name: httpSetKeepAlive
functions.description: Enables or disables HTTP keep-alive on the connection.
requirements: http must be valid
keep_alive must be HTTP_KEEPALIVE_ON or HTTP_KEEPALIVE_OFF

functions.name: httpSetLength
functions.description: Sets the expected content length for the next message body to be sent or received, as appropriate.
requirements: http must be valid
length must be the exact byte count for the body when using Content-Length

functions.name: httpSetTimeout
functions.signature: void httpSetTimeout(http_t *http, double timeout, http_timeout_cb_t cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Sets a per-operation timeout for the connection and an optional callback invoked on timeout events.
requirements: http must be valid
timeout must be non-negative
cb may be NULL or a function matching http_timeout_cb_t; user_data is passed to cb

functions.name: httpShutdown
functions.description: Performs a half or full shutdown of the connection’s underlying socket (implementation-defined) in preparation for close or protocol requirements.
requirements: http must be valid
After shutdown, further I/O may fail; typically followed by httpClose

functions.name: httpStateString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for the given HTTP state value.
requirements: state must be a valid http_state_t value
Returned pointer must not be freed

functions.name: httpStatusString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for the given HTTP status code.
requirements: status must be a valid http_status_t value
Returned pointer must not be freed

functions.name: httpUpdate
functions.description: Processes pending I/O/events on the connection and updates internal state, returning the resulting HTTP status.
requirements: http must be valid
Caller must check the returned status for errors or completion

functions.name: httpURIStatusString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for the given URI parse/assembly status value.
requirements: status must be a valid http_uri_status_t
Returned pointer must not be freed

functions.name: httpWait
functions.description: Waits for the connection to become ready for I/O or for the timeout to elapse.
requirements: http must be valid
msec must be >= 0; 0 may poll immediately
Returns true if ready, false on timeout or error

functions.name: httpWrite
functions.signature: ssize_t httpWrite(http_t *http, const char *buffer, size_t length);
functions.description: Writes up to length bytes from buffer to the connection, following HTTP framing if applicable.
requirements: http must be valid
buffer must point to at least length bytes
Returns number of bytes written or -1 on error; with non-blocking I/O partial writes are possible

functions.name: httpWriteRequest
functions.signature: bool httpWriteRequest(http_t *http, const char *method, const char *uri);
functions.description: Writes an HTTP request line and associated headers for the given method and uri over the connection.
requirements: http must be valid
method must be a valid HTTP method string (e.g., "GET", "POST")
uri must be a valid request-target
Returns true on success, false on failure; caller must follow with any message body writes if needed

functions.name: httpWriteResponse
functions.description: Writes an HTTP response status line and headers for the given status over the connection (server-side use).
requirements: http must be valid
status must be a valid http_status_t to send
Returns true on success, false on failure; caller must write any message body as needed

functions.name: cupsJSONAdd
functions.description: Adds the node to the parent’s child list, inserting it after the specified sibling. Used to build or reorder a JSON tree. Details about whether "after" can be NULL (e.g., to insert at the beginning/end) are not documented here and are inferred from common container APIs.
requirements: parent must be a valid, initialized cups_json_t node representing a container type that can have children (typically array or object); exact allowed types are not documented here.
node must be a valid, initialized cups_json_t not already freed; ownership/lifetime after insertion is not explicitly documented.
If provided, after should be a valid child of parent; behavior when after is NULL or not a child of parent is not specified in this header.
This function does not report errors; callers cannot detect failure via return value.

functions.name: cupsJSONDelete
functions.description: Deletes a JSON node (and typically its subtree). Use to free a tree returned by import or created with cupsJSONNew* APIs. Exact semantics for shared nodes or parent links are not documented here.
requirements: json must be a valid cups_json_t pointer obtained from this API and not previously deleted.
After calling, the json pointer (and any pointers to its children) must not be used.

functions.name: cupsJSONExportFile
functions.description: Serializes the JSON tree to the specified file path. Returns true on success, false on failure.
requirements: json must be a valid cups_json_t pointer to the root (or any node you wish to serialize).
filename must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated path string. The process must have permission to create/overwrite the file as needed.
Callers should check the boolean return value and handle false (failure).

functions.name: cupsJSONExportString
functions.description: Serializes the JSON tree to a newly allocated JSON text string and returns it. Returns NULL on failure. The required deallocation routine for the returned buffer is not specified in this header.
requirements: json must be a valid cups_json_t pointer.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect failure.
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned string; exact function to free (e.g., free vs. a CUPS-specific free) is not documented here and should be verified against the library’s documentation.

functions.name: cupsJSONFind
functions.description: Finds and returns a child/value associated with the given key within an object node. Returns NULL if not found or on error. Exact search scope (direct child vs. recursive) is not specified here and is inferred to be a direct member lookup typical of object maps.
requirements: json should be a valid cups_json_t pointer, typically an object node.
key must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.
Caller must handle a NULL return value.

functions.name: cupsJSONGetChild
functions.description: Returns the n-th child of the given node, or NULL if out of range or on error. Typically used for arrays or objects to iterate children.
requirements: json must be a valid cups_json_t pointer that can have children (array or object).
n should be less than cupsJSONGetCount(json) to avoid out-of-range access; behavior for out-of-range is not documented but is commonly NULL.

functions.name: cupsJSONGetCount
functions.description: Returns the number of children of the node (for arrays/objects). For scalar nodes, the return is typically 0 (inferred).
requirements: json must be a valid cups_json_t pointer.
Caller should not assume non-zero; handle 0 for non-container nodes.

functions.name: cupsJSONGetKey
functions.description: Returns the key string for a key node (object member name). For non-key nodes, may return NULL. Returned pointer is const and owned by the node.
requirements: json must be a valid cups_json_t pointer.
Caller must not modify or free the returned string; its lifetime is tied to the node.
Caller must handle possible NULL return.

functions.name: cupsJSONGetParent
functions.description: Returns the parent node of the given node, or NULL if the node is a root or on error.
requirements: json must be a valid cups_json_t pointer.
Caller must handle a NULL return value.

functions.name: cupsJSONGetSibling
functions.description: Returns the next sibling of the given node, or NULL if none. Useful for iterating children via linked-list style traversal.
requirements: json must be a valid cups_json_t pointer that is part of a parent’s child list.
Caller must handle a NULL return value.

functions.name: cupsJSONGetNumber
functions.description: Returns the numeric value of a number node as a double. Behavior for non-number nodes is not specified here (commonly 0.0).
requirements: json must be a valid cups_json_t pointer, typically of type CUPS_JTYPE_NUMBER.
Callers should ensure the node type is numeric (e.g., via cupsJSONGetType) before calling to avoid undefined or lossy conversions.

functions.name: cupsJSONGetString
functions.description: Returns the string value for a string node (and possibly for key nodes). Returns NULL if the node is not a string or on error. The returned pointer is const and owned by the node.
requirements: json must be a valid cups_json_t pointer.
Caller must not modify or free the returned string; its lifetime is tied to the node.
Caller must handle a NULL return value.
Callers should verify node type (e.g., CUPS_JTYPE_STRING) before calling when strict type handling is required.

functions.name: cupsJSONGetType
functions.description: Returns the type of the JSON node as a cups_jtype_t enum value.
requirements: json must be a valid cups_json_t pointer.

functions.name: cupsJSONImportFile
functions.description: Parses JSON from a file and returns the root node of the parsed tree on success, or NULL on error.
requirements: filename must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated path to a readable file containing JSON.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect parse or I/O failure.
The returned tree must be freed by the caller using cupsJSONDelete when no longer needed.

functions.name: cupsJSONImportString
functions.description: Parses JSON from a NUL-terminated string and returns the root node on success, or NULL on error.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing JSON text.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect parse failure.
The returned tree must be freed by the caller using cupsJSONDelete when no longer needed.

functions.name: cupsJSONImportURL
functions.description: Fetches JSON from the given URL and parses it, returning the root node on success, or NULL on error. If provided, last_modified may be set to the server’s Last-Modified time (inferred). Network/transport details and authentication are not specified here.
requirements: url must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated URL string.
last_modified may be NULL or a valid pointer to time_t storage for output; exact semantics are not documented here.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect fetch/parse failure.
The returned tree must be freed by the caller using cupsJSONDelete when no longer needed.

functions.name: cupsJSONNew
functions.description: Creates a new JSON node of the specified type and (optionally) inserts it under parent after the given sibling. Returns the new node or NULL on failure. Exact rules for which types are allowed under which parents are not specified here.
requirements: type must be a valid cups_jtype_t value.
If parent is non-NULL, it must be a valid container node (typically array or object) from this API; exact allowed types are not documented here.
If provided, after should be a valid child of parent; behavior when after is NULL or invalid is unspecified in this header.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation/insert failure.

functions.name: cupsJSONNewKey
functions.description: Creates a new key node with the provided key string and (optionally) inserts it under parent after the given sibling. Returns the new node or NULL on failure. Typically used when constructing object members; exact insertion semantics are not fully documented here.
requirements: key must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
If parent is non-NULL, it must be a valid container that accepts keys (typically an object).
If provided, after should be a valid child of parent; behavior when after is NULL or invalid is unspecified.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation/insert failure.

functions.name: cupsJSONNewNumber
functions.description: Creates a new numeric node with the given value and (optionally) inserts it under parent after the given sibling. Returns the new node or NULL on failure.
requirements: If parent is non-NULL, it must be a valid container node (array/object).
If provided, after should be a valid child of parent; behavior when after is NULL or invalid is unspecified.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation/insert failure.

functions.name: cupsJSONNewString
functions.description: Creates a new string node with the given value and (optionally) inserts it under parent after the given sibling. Returns the new node or NULL on failure.
requirements: value must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
If parent is non-NULL, it must be a valid container node (array/object).
If provided, after should be a valid child of parent; behavior when after is NULL or invalid is unspecified.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation/insert failure.

functions.name: cupsJWTDelete
functions.description: Destroys a JWT object and releases any resources it holds. Use after finishing with a token created/imported via cupsJWTNew or cupsJWTImportString.
requirements: jwt must be a valid pointer returned by cupsJWTNew or cupsJWTImportString, or NULL (passing NULL is a no-op).
The jwt pointer must not be used after this call (dangling pointer).

functions.name: cupsJWTExportString
functions.description: Serializes the JWT to a string using the specified JWS serialization format (compact or JSON). Returns a newly allocated string containing the encoded token.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
format must be a valid cups_jws_format_t value (e.g., CUPS_JWS_FORMAT_COMPACT or CUPS_JWS_FORMAT_JSON).
On success, the caller owns the returned string; memory management of the returned buffer is unspecified in this header (likely heap-allocated).
Function may return NULL on error; callers must handle a NULL return.

functions.name: cupsJWTGetAlgorithm
functions.description: Returns the algorithm (JWA) associated with the JWT’s signature/header.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
If the JWT is unsigned or lacks an algorithm, the function may return CUPS_JWA_NONE.

functions.name: cupsJWTGetClaimNumber
functions.description: Retrieves a numeric claim value as a double from the JWT payload for the given claim name (e.g., exp, iat).
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming a claim.
Behavior/return value for missing or non-numeric claims is unspecified by this header; callers must be prepared for default/zero or special values.

functions.name: cupsJWTGetClaimString
functions.description: Retrieves a string claim value from the JWT payload for the given claim name. Returns a pointer to the string value.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming a claim.
The lifetime/ownership of the returned pointer is unspecified; it may be owned by the JWT and become invalid after modifications or deletion of the jwt.
Function may return NULL if the claim is missing or not a string; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: cupsJWTGetClaimType
functions.description: Returns the JSON type of the specified claim in the JWT payload (e.g., string, number, boolean, object, array, null).
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming a claim.

functions.name: cupsJWTGetClaimValue
functions.description: Returns the raw JSON value node for the specified claim in the JWT payload.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming a claim.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned cups_json_t* is unspecified; it may be an internal pointer and must not be freed or modified unless documented elsewhere.
Function may return NULL if the claim does not exist.

functions.name: cupsJWTGetClaims
functions.description: Returns the JSON object that contains all claims (the JWT payload).
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned cups_json_t* is unspecified; it may be internal to jwt and not to be freed by the caller.
Function may return NULL on error or if claims are unavailable.

functions.name: cupsJWTGetHeaderNumber
functions.description: Retrieves a numeric value from the JWT header for the given parameter name as a double.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming a header parameter.
Behavior/return for missing or non-numeric values is unspecified; callers must handle default/zero or special values.

functions.name: cupsJWTGetHeaderString
functions.description: Retrieves a string value from the JWT header for the given parameter name. Returns a pointer to the string value.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming a header parameter.
The lifetime/ownership of the returned pointer is unspecified; it may be owned by the JWT and invalidated after modifications or deletion of jwt.
Function may return NULL if the header parameter is missing or not a string.

functions.name: cupsJWTGetHeaderType
functions.description: Returns the JSON type of the specified JWT header parameter.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming a header parameter.

functions.name: cupsJWTGetHeaderValue
functions.description: Returns the raw JSON value node for the specified JWT header parameter.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming a header parameter.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned cups_json_t* is unspecified; it may be internal to jwt and not to be freed or modified by the caller.
Function may return NULL if the parameter does not exist.

functions.name: cupsJWTGetHeaders
functions.description: Returns the JSON object that contains all JWT header parameters.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned cups_json_t* is unspecified; it may be internal to jwt and not to be freed by the caller.
Function may return NULL on error or if headers are unavailable.

functions.name: cupsJWTHasValidSignature
functions.description: Verifies the JWT’s signature using the provided keys (likely a JWK or JWK Set). Returns true if the signature is valid for one of the keys.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
keys must be a cups_json_t* referencing appropriate key material; exact structure is not specified here (likely JWK/JWK Set).
Returns false on invalid signature or error; callers must handle a false result.

functions.name: cupsJWTImportString
functions.description: Parses and imports a JWT from a string in the specified JWS serialization format and returns a new JWT object.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing a JWT in the specified format.
format must be a valid cups_jws_format_t value.
Returns NULL on parse/validation error; callers must handle NULL.
The returned jwt must be released with cupsJWTDelete when no longer needed.

functions.name: cupsJWTLoadCredentials
functions.description: Loads credentials (likely keys/certificates) from the given filesystem path, optionally filtered or matched by common_name, and returns them as a JSON structure (e.g., JWK/JWK Set).
requirements: path must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated filesystem path string.
common_name may be NULL or a NUL-terminated string; exact matching semantics are unspecified.
Returns NULL on error; callers must handle NULL.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned cups_json_t* is unspecified here; typically caller would manage and later free via the CUPS JSON API.

functions.name: cupsJWTMakePrivateKey
functions.description: Generates a new private key suitable for the specified JWA algorithm and returns it as a JSON Web Key (JWK) object.
requirements: alg must be a valid cups_jwa_t value indicating a supported asymmetric or HMAC algorithm.
Returns NULL on error or unsupported algorithm; callers must handle NULL.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned cups_json_t* is unspecified here; typically caller would manage via the CUPS JSON API.

functions.name: cupsJWTMakePublicKey
functions.description: Derives a public key JWK from the provided private key JWK and returns it as a JSON object.
requirements: jwk must be a valid cups_json_t* representing a private key JWK; exact schema is not specified here.
Returns NULL on error or if input is not a suitable private key; callers must handle NULL.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned cups_json_t* is unspecified here; typically caller would manage via the CUPS JSON API.

functions.name: cupsJWTNew
functions.description: Creates a new JWT object with the given type (e.g., the typ header) and initial claims JSON object.
requirements: type may be NULL or a NUL-terminated string indicating the JWT type; exact allowed values are not specified.
claims may be NULL or a cups_json_t* JSON object representing initial claims; structure not specified.
Returns NULL on error; callers must handle NULL.
The returned jwt must be released with cupsJWTDelete when no longer needed.
Ownership transfer rules for the claims object are unspecified; callers should not assume claims are consumed or cloned without consulting implementation docs.

functions.name: cupsJWTSetClaimNumber
functions.signature: void cupsJWTSetClaimNumber(cups_jwt_t *jwt, const char *claim, double value);
functions.description: Sets or replaces a numeric claim in the JWT payload to the specified double value.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming the claim to set.

functions.name: cupsJWTSetClaimString
functions.signature: void cupsJWTSetClaimString(cups_jwt_t *jwt, const char *claim, const char *value);
functions.description: Sets or replaces a string claim in the JWT payload to the specified string value.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming the claim to set.
value must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: cupsJWTSetClaimValue
functions.description: Sets or replaces a claim in the JWT payload using a provided JSON value node.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming the claim to set.
value must be a valid cups_json_t* JSON value; exact allowed types depend on claim semantics and are not specified.
Ownership/retention of value is unspecified; caller should not free or modify value if adopted by jwt without consulting implementation docs.

functions.name: cupsJWTSetHeaderNumber
functions.signature: void cupsJWTSetHeaderNumber(cups_jwt_t *jwt, const char *claim, double value);
functions.description: Sets or replaces a numeric parameter in the JWT header to the specified double value.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming the header parameter to set.

functions.name: cupsJWTSetHeaderString
functions.signature: void cupsJWTSetHeaderString(cups_jwt_t *jwt, const char *claim, const char *value);
functions.description: Sets or replaces a string parameter in the JWT header to the specified string value.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming the header parameter to set.
value must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: cupsJWTSetHeaderValue
functions.description: Sets or replaces a header parameter in the JWT header using a provided JSON value node.
requirements: jwt must be a valid, initialized JWT object.
claim must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming the header parameter to set.
value must be a valid cups_json_t* JSON value; exact allowed types depend on parameter semantics and are not specified.

functions.name: cupsJWTSign

functions.name: cupsOAuthClearTokens

functions.name: cupsOAuthCopyAccessToken

functions.name: cupsOAuthCopyClientId

functions.signature: cups_json_t *cupsOAuthGetDeviceGrant(const char *auth_uri, cups_json_t *metadata, const char *resource_uri, const char *scopes)

functions.name: cupsOAuthGetJWKS
functions.description: Fetches the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) for the authorization server and returns it as a JSON object suitable for JWT verification. Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cupsOAuthGetTokens
functions.signature: char *cupsOAuthGetTokens(const char *auth_uri, cups_json_t *metadata, const char *resource_uri, const char *grant_code, cups_ogrant_t grant_type, const char *redirect_uri, time_t *access_expires)
functions.description: Exchanges a grant (authorization code, device code, or refresh token) for tokens with the authorization server. requirements: auth_uri must be a valid, null-terminated URI string for the authorization server.

functions.name: cupsOAuthGetUserId

requirements: auth_uri must be a valid, null-terminated URI string for the authorization server.

functions.name: cupsOAuthMakeAuthorizationURL
functions.signature: char *cupsOAuthMakeAuthorizationURL(const char *auth_uri, cups_json_t *metadata, const char *resource_uri, const char *scopes, const char *client_id, const char *code_verifier, const char *nonce, const char *redirect_uri, const char *state)

requirements: auth_uri must be a valid, null-terminated URI string for the authorization server.
metadata must be a valid cups_json_t metadata object for auth_uri (from cupsOAuthGetMetadata) and must remain valid during the call.

functions.name: cupsOAuthMakeBase64Random
functions.description: Generates and returns a newly allocated, base64 (likely URL-safe) string derived from len bytes of cryptographically random data. Useful for PKCE code_verifier, nonce, or state parameters. Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cupsOAuthSaveClientData

functions.name: cupsOAuthSaveTokens

requirements: auth_uri must be a valid, null-terminated URI string for the authorization server.

functions.name: pwgFormatSizeName
functions.signature: bool pwgFormatSizeName(char *keyword, size_t keysize, const char *prefix, const char *name, int width, int length, const char *units);
functions.description: Formats a PWG media size keyword string from the given components and writes it into the provided buffer. Typical usage is to build a stable media keyword (e.g., for IPP/PPD/PWG) using a namespace prefix and a human/legacy name combined with explicit dimensions. Returns true on success and false on failure (e.g., if the buffer is too small or inputs are invalid). Notes: The exact expected values/format for prefix/name/units are not documented here; dimensions are integers and commonly represent 1/100 mm units (2540 units per inch) in CUPS PWG code, but this function accepts an explicit units string; details are unknown if units is NULL or unrecognized.
requirements: keyword must be a valid, writable buffer pointer.
keysize must be the number of bytes available at keyword and must be large enough to hold the resulting NUL-terminated keyword.
prefix should be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string identifying a namespace or family (exact allowed values unknown).
name should be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string (exact format/allowed characters unknown).

width and length are integer dimensions; in CUPS PWG structures dimensions are commonly in hundredths of millimeters (2540 per inch); if units specifies another system, width/length should match that units system (exact accepted units strings are unknown).
units should be a NUL-terminated string describing the units for width/length (exact accepted values are unknown).
The output string written to keyword will be NUL-terminated on success; callers should not assume modification on failure and should check the return value.

functions.name: pwgInitSize
functions.description: Initializes a pwg_size_t structure from IPP job/printer attributes, computing media width/length and margins. Returns true on success and false on failure (e.g., missing or inconsistent attributes). If margins_set is provided, it is set to indicate whether margins were determined from job attributes. Notes: Requires CUPS/IPP types (ipp_t). Exact attribute names consulted are not specified here.
requirements: size must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a pwg_size_t structure that the function will initialize.

On success, width/length and margin fields of size are populated in 1/100 mm units (2540 per inch), consistent with pwg_size_t definition.
Callers must check the boolean return value before using the initialized size.

functions.name: pwgMediaForLegacy
functions.description: Looks up media information by an IPP/ISO legacy media name and returns a pointer to the corresponding pwg_media_t record (containing PWG keyword, legacy name, PPD name, width, and length). Returns NULL if no match is found. The returned pointer refers to internal/static data and must not be modified or freed.
requirements: legacy must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string representing a legacy media name.

functions.name: pwgMediaForPPD
functions.description: Looks up media information by an Adobe PPD media name and returns a pointer to the corresponding pwg_media_t record. Returns NULL if no match is found. The returned pointer refers to internal/static data and must not be modified or freed.
requirements: ppd must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string representing a PPD media name.
Callers must check for a NULL return to handle the not-found case.
The returned pwg_media_t pointer is owned by the library; do not free or modify it.
