functions.name: pwgMediaForSize
functions.description: Finds a media entry whose dimensions match the given width and length and returns a pointer to the corresponding pwg_media_t record. Dimensions are in 1/100 mm units (2540 units per inch), consistent with PWG/CUPS media definitions. Returns NULL if no match is found. The returned pointer refers to internal/static data and must not be modified or freed.
requirements: width and length must be positive integers expressed in hundredths of millimeters (2540 per inch).
Callers must check for a NULL return to handle the not-found case.
The returned pwg_media_t pointer is owned by the library; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: cupsRasterClose

functions.name: cupsRasterGetErrorString

functions.name: cupsRasterInitHeader
functions.signature: extern bool cupsRasterInitHeader(cups_page_header_t *h, cups_media_t *media, const char *optimize, ipp_quality_t quality, const char *intent, ipp_orient_t orientation, const char *sides, const char *type, int xdpi, int ydpi, const char *sheet_back) _CUPS_PUBLIC;

If strings is non-NULL, it must point to a null-terminated buffer containing valid CUPS catalog data.
Behavior when both filename and strings are NULL is unspecified in this header; callers should pass at least one non-NULL source.
Return value is true on success and false on failure; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: cupsLangPrintf
functions.description: Writes a localized, formatted message to the given FILE stream, similar to fprintf with localization support. Returns the number of bytes written, or a negative value on error. Use for emitting localized output to files or stdout/stderr.
requirements: fp must be a valid, open FILE pointer for output.
format must be a non-NULL, null-terminated format string; varargs must match the format specifiers.
Callers must check the return value: a negative value indicates an output error.
Thread-safety and locale handling semantics are not specified in this header; avoid concurrent writes to the same FILE without external synchronization.

functions.name: cupsLangPuts
functions.description: Writes the provided message (after localization handling as applicable) to the given FILE stream, similar to fputs but returning ssize_t. Returns the number of bytes written, or a negative value on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid, open FILE pointer for output.
message must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string.
Callers must check the return value: a negative value indicates an output error.

functions.name: cupsLangSetDirectory
functions.description: Sets the directory where CUPS looks for localization/message catalog files. Use to override the default message catalog search path.
requirements: d should be a non-NULL, null-terminated pathname string. Whether NULL is accepted to reset to a default is unknown from this header.
The path must reference a directory accessible to the process; permission and existence checks are not specified here.

functions.name: cupsLangSetLocale
functions.description: Initializes/adjusts the process locale for CUPS based on command-line arguments (typically the argv from main). May modify argv entries to reflect locale processing. Use early in program startup to configure localization behavior.
requirements: argv should be the process argument vector as passed to main; it must be a NULL-terminated array of pointers.
Because the parameter is non-const, callers should assume the function may modify the provided strings or vector; supply writable storage for argv and its strings.
Behavior when argv is NULL is unspecified; pass a valid argument vector.

functions.name: cupsFileClose
functions.description: Closes a CUPS file stream and releases associated resources/buffers. Typically used on cups_file_t objects obtained from cupsFileOpen, cupsFileOpenFd, cupsFileStdin, cupsFileStdout, or cupsFileStderr.
requirements: fp must be a valid cups_file_t pointer obtained from a CUPS file open/constructor function.
Do not use fp after successful close.

functions.name: cupsFileEOF
functions.description: Reports whether the end-of-file condition has been reached on the given CUPS file stream.
requirements: fp must be a valid, initialized cups_file_t pointer.

functions.name: cupsFileFind
functions.signature: const char *cupsFileFind(const char *filename, const char *path, bool executable, char *buffer, size_t bufsize)
functions.description: Searches for filename in a path list and returns the resolved path. When found, the resulting path is written to buffer and the returned pointer references it. The search may respect the executable flag to restrict results to executable files.
requirements: filename must be a non-null C string.
path must be a non-null C string containing one or more search directories (format unspecified).
buffer must be non-null and point to a writable array of at least bufsize bytes.
bufsize must be greater than 0.
If executable is true, callers should expect non-executable files to be ignored.
Caller must not use the returned pointer after buffer goes out of scope.

functions.name: cupsFileFlush
functions.description: Flushes any buffered output for the given CUPS file stream to the underlying file descriptor/device.
requirements: fp must be a valid cups_file_t pointer opened in a mode that permits writing for flush to have an effect.

functions.name: cupsFileGetChar
functions.description: Reads the next byte from the CUPS file stream and returns it as an unsigned-char value promoted to int, or a negative value on EOF/error.
requirements: fp must be a valid, readable cups_file_t pointer.

functions.name: cupsFileGetConf
functions.signature: char *cupsFileGetConf(cups_file_t *fp, char *buf, size_t buflen, char **value, int *linenum)
functions.description: Parses the next non-comment configuration line from the CUPS file stream. Writes the directive/token into buf and sets *value to the value portion (typically within buf). Updates *linenum with the current line number. Returns buf on success or NULL on EOF/error. Specific parsing rules are not documented here and may follow CUPS config conventions (unknown details).
requirements: fp must be a valid, readable cups_file_t pointer.
buf must be non-null and point to a writable array of at least buflen bytes.
buflen must be greater than 0.
value may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to a char* variable to receive a pointer within buf.
linenum may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to an int to receive/track the current line number.

functions.name: cupsFileGetLine
functions.description: Reads a line of text from the CUPS file stream into buf, up to buflen-1 bytes, and NUL-terminates it. Returns the number of bytes stored (excluding the NUL). Line-ending handling follows CUPS file semantics (may normalize CR, CRLF, LF).
requirements: fp must be a valid, readable cups_file_t pointer.
buf must be non-null and point to a writable array of at least buflen bytes.
buflen must be greater than 0.

functions.name: cupsFileGets
functions.description: Reads a line of text from the CUPS file stream into buf and NUL-terminates it. Returns buf on success or NULL on EOF/error. May handle different line endings transparently.
requirements: fp must be a valid, readable cups_file_t pointer.
buf must be non-null and point to a writable array of at least buflen bytes.
buflen must be greater than 0.

functions.name: cupsFileIsCompressed
functions.description: Indicates whether the CUPS file stream represents a compressed file (e.g., gzip) being handled transparently by the CUPS I/O layer.
requirements: fp must be a valid cups_file_t pointer.

functions.name: cupsFileLock
functions.description: Attempts to place an advisory lock on the underlying file for the CUPS file stream. If block is true, the call may wait until the lock can be acquired.
requirements: fp must be a valid cups_file_t pointer referencing a real file that supports locking.
Callers should avoid deadlocks when block is true.
Locking semantics (shared/exclusive) are unspecified here (unknown).

functions.name: cupsFileNumber
functions.description: Returns the underlying file descriptor number associated with the CUPS file stream, or a negative value on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid cups_file_t pointer.

functions.name: cupsFileOpen
functions.description: Opens a file by name using CUPS I/O semantics (transparent line-endings, optional compression handling) and returns a CUPS file stream handle.
requirements: filename must be a non-null C string naming the file to open.
mode must be a non-null C string specifying the open mode (syntax follows C stdio-like modes; exact accepted flags are not documented here).
On success, the returned cups_file_t* must be closed with cupsFileClose.

functions.name: cupsFileOpenFd
functions.description: Wraps an existing file descriptor in a CUPS file stream handle with the specified mode, enabling CUPS I/O semantics on that descriptor.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open file descriptor compatible with the requested mode.
mode must be a non-null C string specifying how the stream should be used (read/write, etc.; exact syntax unspecified here).
On success, the returned cups_file_t* must be closed with cupsFileClose. The wrapper may (or may not) close fd on close (behavior unspecified here; unknown).

functions.name: cupsFilePeekChar
functions.description: Returns the next byte from the CUPS file stream without consuming it, or a negative value on EOF/error.
requirements: fp must be a valid, readable cups_file_t pointer.

functions.name: cupsFilePrintf
functions.description: Writes formatted text to the CUPS file stream using printf-style formatting. Returns true on success, false on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid, writable cups_file_t pointer.
format must be a non-null C string; additional arguments must match the format specifiers.
Caller should check the boolean return for success/failure.

functions.name: cupsFilePutChar
functions.description: Writes a single byte (low 8 bits of c) to the CUPS file stream. Returns true on success, false on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid, writable cups_file_t pointer.

functions.name: cupsFilePutConf
functions.signature: bool cupsFilePutConf(cups_file_t *fp, const char *directive, const char *value)
functions.description: Writes a configuration line consisting of a directive and value to the CUPS file stream, following CUPS config file syntax (exact formatting rules not specified here; unknown details).
requirements: fp must be a valid, writable cups_file_t pointer.
directive must be a non-null C string.
value may be NULL or a C string depending on directive; exact requirements unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: cupsFilePuts
functions.description: Writes a NUL-terminated string to the CUPS file stream. Returns true on success, false on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid, writable cups_file_t pointer.
s must be a non-null C string.

functions.name: cupsFileRead
functions.description: Reads up to bytes bytes from the CUPS file stream into buf. Returns the number of bytes read, 0 on EOF, or a negative value on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid, readable cups_file_t pointer.
buf must be non-null and point to a writable array of at least bytes bytes.
bytes may be zero; if zero, no data is read.

functions.name: cupsFileRewind
functions.description: Seeks the CUPS file stream to the beginning (offset 0) and returns the resulting offset, or a negative value on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid cups_file_t pointer referencing a seekable stream.

functions.name: cupsFileSeek
functions.description: Seeks the CUPS file stream to the specified absolute byte offset and returns the resulting offset, or a negative value on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid cups_file_t pointer referencing a seekable stream.
pos should be a non-negative file offset supported by the underlying file/device.

functions.name: cupsFileStderr
functions.description: Returns a CUPS file stream wrapper for the process standard error (stderr).
requirements: Returned handle should be treated as a CUPS-managed wrapper; do not close underlying OS handle directly.
The returned handle must be closed with cupsFileClose when no longer needed (behavior in some environments may share a global wrapper; specifics unknown).

functions.name: cupsFileStdin
functions.description: Returns a CUPS file stream wrapper for the process standard input (stdin).
requirements: Returned handle should be treated as a CUPS-managed wrapper; do not close underlying OS handle directly.
The returned handle must be closed with cupsFileClose when no longer needed (behavior may be implementation-defined; specifics unknown).

functions.name: cupsFileStdout
functions.description: Returns a CUPS file stream wrapper for the process standard output (stdout).
requirements: Returned handle should be treated as a CUPS-managed wrapper; do not close underlying OS handle directly.
The returned handle must be closed with cupsFileClose when no longer needed (behavior may be implementation-defined; specifics unknown).

functions.name: cupsFileTell
functions.description: Returns the current byte offset of the CUPS file stream, or a negative value on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid cups_file_t pointer referencing a seekable stream.

functions.name: cupsFileUnlock
functions.description: Releases a previously acquired file lock on the CUPS file stream.
requirements: fp must be a valid cups_file_t pointer for which a lock may have been acquired via cupsFileLock.

functions.name: cupsFileWrite
functions.signature: bool cupsFileWrite(cups_file_t *fp, const char *buf, size_t bytes)
functions.description: Writes bytes bytes from buf to the CUPS file stream. Returns true on success, false on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid, writable cups_file_t pointer.
buf must be non-null and point to at least bytes bytes of data.
bytes may be zero; if zero, no data is written.
Caller should check the boolean return for success/failure.

functions.name: cupsFormDecode
functions.description: Decode application/x-www-form-urlencoded form data into a CUPS option array. Given a NUL-terminated form string (e.g., "name=Alice&count=3"), this function parses the key/value pairs and outputs them as a dynamically allocated array of cups_option_t via vars. Returns the number of parsed options. Typical usage is to pass the incoming form body and then use other CUPS option helpers to read values; free the resulting options when done. Parsing and exact decoding rules are not documented here; details such as percent-decoding and plus-to-space behavior are inferred but not guaranteed by this header.
requirements: data must point to a valid NUL-terminated string containing form-encoded data (inferred from the function name and signature).
vars must be non-NULL and point to a cups_option_t* receiver that will be set to an allocated array of options (inferred from signature).
The returned count is the number of options written to *vars; if zero, *vars may be left as NULL or an empty allocation (exact behavior unknown).
Caller must release the allocated options array when finished; typical CUPS convention is cupsFreeOptions(count, *vars) (inferred from CUPS option APIs).
This function does not expose an explicit error code; callers should treat a return value of 0 as "no options or parse failure"; precise error signaling is unknown.

functions.name: cupsFormEncode
functions.description: Encode cups_option_t key/value pairs as application/x-www-form-urlencoded data, optionally combined with a base URL. Given num_vars entries in vars, returns a newly allocated string containing the encoded form data; if url is provided, the result is expected to be the URL with the query string appended (exact formatting unspecified in this header). Use when constructing HTTP form submissions or URLs with query parameters based on CUPS options.
requirements: If num_vars > 0, vars must point to an array of at least num_vars valid cups_option_t entries (inferred from signature).
If num_vars == 0, vars may be NULL (inferred).
url may be NULL to request only a raw form-encoded string; if non-NULL, it is treated as a base URL to which encoded parameters are applied (inferred from parameter name and common patterns).
The returned string is dynamically allocated; the caller must free it when done (typical CUPS convention is standard free(), inference).
Keys and values in vars must be valid NUL-terminated strings suitable for URL/form encoding; behavior for NULL pointers inside vars is undefined (inferred).
On failure, the function may return NULL; callers must check for NULL before use (inferred).

functions.name: cupsCharsetToUTF8
functions.signature: ssize_t cupsCharsetToUTF8(char *dest, const char *src, const size_t maxout, const cups_encoding_t encoding);
functions.description: Converts a text string from the specified single-/multi-byte character set (encoding) to UTF-8 and writes the result to dest. Typical usage is to transcode input in a known legacy encoding to UTF-8 before further processing. Returns a size value (likely the number of bytes written) or a negative value on failure; exact return semantics are not documented here.
requirements: dest must point to a writable buffer with capacity of at least maxout bytes.
src must point to a NUL-terminated string encoded using the specified encoding.
maxout specifies the maximum number of output bytes that may be written to dest and must not exceed the actual capacity of dest.
encoding must be a valid cups_encoding_t value; handling of CUPS_ENCODING_AUTO is not defined in this header.
Behavior on insufficient space (truncation vs. error) and whether a NUL terminator is always written are not specified and should be confirmed from implementation or broader CUPS documentation.

functions.name: cupsEncodingString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable name (string) for the given cups_encoding_t value. Used to map an encoding enum to its string representation for display or configuration.
requirements: value must be a cups_encoding_t enumerator. Behavior for out-of-range values is not documented.
The returned pointer refers to memory managed by the library; ownership and lifetime are not documented here—treat as read-only and non-modifiable.

functions.name: cupsEncodingValue
functions.description: Parses a string naming a character set/encoding and returns the corresponding cups_encoding_t value. Useful for interpreting configuration or user-provided encoding names.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated C string. Acceptable name formats and case-sensitivity are not documented here.
Return value for unknown or unsupported names is not specified in this header (could be a specific enumerator or a default). Callers should be prepared to handle an unspecified/invalid result.

functions.name: cupsUTF8ToCharset
functions.signature: ssize_t cupsUTF8ToCharset(char *dest, const char *src, const size_t maxout, const cups_encoding_t encoding);
functions.description: Converts a UTF-8 encoded text string to the specified target character set (encoding) and writes the result to dest. Commonly used to generate output in a legacy or device-required encoding. Returns a size value (likely number of bytes written) or a negative value on failure; exact return semantics are not documented here.
requirements: dest must point to a writable buffer with capacity of at least maxout bytes.
src must point to a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.
maxout specifies the maximum number of output bytes that may be written to dest and must not exceed the actual capacity of dest.
encoding must be a valid cups_encoding_t value; behavior for encodings that cannot represent certain UTF-8 code points is not specified here (error vs. substitution).
Behavior on insufficient space (truncation vs. error) and whether a NUL terminator is always written are not specified and should be confirmed from implementation or broader CUPS documentation.

functions.name: cupsUTF8ToUTF32
functions.signature: ssize_t cupsUTF8ToUTF32(cups_utf32_t *dest, const char *src, const size_t maxout);
functions.description: Converts a UTF-8 encoded string to UTF-32 code units (cups_utf32_t) and writes them to dest. Useful for code-point level processing. Returns a size value (likely the number of UTF-32 code units written) or a negative value on failure; exact return semantics are not documented here.
requirements: dest must point to a writable array of cups_utf32_t with capacity for at least maxout elements.
src must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.
maxout specifies the maximum number of UTF-32 code units that may be written to dest and must not exceed the actual capacity of dest.
Whether a terminating 0 code unit is written and how invalid UTF-8 sequences are handled are not specified here.

functions.name: cupsUTF32ToUTF8
functions.signature: ssize_t cupsUTF32ToUTF8(char *dest, const cups_utf32_t *src, const size_t maxout);
functions.description: Converts a UTF-32 code unit sequence (cups_utf32_t) to UTF-8 and writes the result to dest. Useful for serializing Unicode code points into UTF-8. Returns a size value (likely the number of bytes written) or a negative value on failure; exact return semantics are not documented here.
requirements: dest must point to a writable buffer with capacity of at least maxout bytes.
src must point to a UTF-32 sequence terminated by a 0 code unit (typical for C-style UTF-32 strings); this is inferred and not explicitly documented.
maxout specifies the maximum number of UTF-8 bytes that may be written to dest and must not exceed the actual capacity of dest.
Handling of invalid code points, surrogate ranges, and whether a NUL terminator is always written are not specified here.

functions.name: cupsThreadGetData
functions.signature: macro: cupsThreadGetData(cups_thread_key_t key) -> platform-dependent return type (void* on POSIX; LPVOID/void* on Windows)
functions.description: Returns the thread-local value associated with the given thread data key for the calling thread. This is a macro that maps to pthread_getspecific (POSIX) or TlsGetValue (Windows). Use it to retrieve per-thread data previously set for the same key.
requirements: key must be a valid cups_thread_key_t created/initialized for thread-local storage prior to use (from the appropriate CUPS or platform TLS key creation API; not shown here).
Must be called by a running thread context; key is per-thread.
Caller must handle platform-specific error/NULL semantics (e.g., NULL may be a valid stored value; underlying API provides error via errno/GetLastError).

functions.name: cupsThreadSetData
functions.signature: macro: cupsThreadSetData(cups_thread_key_t key, void *ptr) -> platform-dependent return type (int on POSIX; BOOL on Windows)
functions.description: Associates a thread-local value with the given thread data key for the calling thread. This is a macro that maps to pthread_setspecific (POSIX) or TlsSetValue (Windows).
requirements: key must be a valid cups_thread_key_t created/initialized for thread-local storage prior to use.
May be called with ptr == NULL to clear the current value (supported by underlying APIs).
Caller must check the platform-specific return code for success/failure (0 on success for pthread_setspecific; nonzero/BOOL for Windows).
If a destructor was registered for the key (outside this header), it will apply per-thread when the thread exits (platform behavior).

functions.name: cupsCondBroadcast
functions.description: Wakes all threads waiting on the specified condition variable. Typically used after updating shared state protected by a mutex so that all waiting threads can recheck their predicates.
requirements: cond must point to an initialized cups_cond_t.
Should be called while holding the associated mutex protecting the condition predicate (typical condition variable usage).

functions.name: cupsCondDestroy
functions.description: Destroys a condition variable and releases any underlying resources.
requirements: cond must point to an initialized cups_cond_t.
No threads may be waiting on cond at the time of destruction.
Must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: cupsCondInit
functions.description: Initializes a condition variable for use with cupsCondWait and cupsCondBroadcast.
requirements: cond must be a valid pointer to storage for a cups_cond_t.
Must be called exactly once before using the condition variable.
Do not re-initialize an already initialized condition variable without destroying it first.

functions.name: cupsCondWait
functions.signature: extern void cupsCondWait(cups_cond_t *cond, cups_mutex_t *mutex, double timeout);
functions.description: Waits on the condition variable until signaled/broadcast or until the timeout elapses. The mutex is atomically released while waiting and re-acquired before return. The timeout is expressed in seconds; exact semantics for non-positive values are not documented here.
requirements: cond must point to an initialized cups_cond_t.
mutex must point to an initialized cups_mutex_t and must be locked by the calling thread prior to calling.
Caller should treat wakeups as potentially spurious and re-check the predicate on return (typical condition variable practice).
timeout must be provided in seconds; specific allowed ranges and special values are not documented in this header.

functions.name: cupsMutexDestroy
functions.description: Destroys a mutex and releases any underlying resources.
requirements: mutex must point to an initialized cups_mutex_t.
The mutex must not be locked by any thread at the time of destruction.
Must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: cupsMutexInit
functions.description: Initializes a mutex for mutual exclusion.
requirements: mutex must be a valid pointer to storage for a cups_mutex_t.
Must be called exactly once before using the mutex.
Do not re-initialize an already initialized mutex without destroying it first.

functions.name: cupsMutexLock
functions.description: Locks the specified mutex, blocking if necessary until it becomes available.
requirements: mutex must point to an initialized cups_mutex_t.
Each successful lock must be paired with a corresponding cupsMutexUnlock by the same thread.
Do not attempt to lock a mutex already locked by the same thread unless the implementation supports recursive behavior (not specified here).

functions.name: cupsMutexUnlock
functions.description: Unlocks a previously locked mutex.
requirements: mutex must point to an initialized cups_mutex_t.
The calling thread must currently hold the lock on the mutex.
Each unlock should correspond to a prior successful cupsMutexLock by the same thread.

functions.name: cupsRWDestroy
functions.description: Destroys a reader/writer lock and releases any underlying resources.
requirements: rwlock must point to an initialized cups_rwlock_t.
No thread may hold the lock (read or write) at the time of destruction.
Must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: cupsRWInit
functions.description: Initializes a reader/writer lock for use with read or write locking.
requirements: rwlock must be a valid pointer to storage for a cups_rwlock_t.
Must be called exactly once before using the lock.
Do not re-initialize an already initialized lock without destroying it first.

functions.name: cupsRWLockRead
functions.description: Acquires the lock for shared (reader) access, allowing multiple readers concurrently.
requirements: rwlock must point to an initialized cups_rwlock_t.
Each successful read lock must be paired with a corresponding cupsRWUnlock by the same thread.
May block if a writer holds or is waiting for the lock (typical RW-lock behavior).

functions.name: cupsRWLockWrite
functions.description: Acquires the lock for exclusive (writer) access.
requirements: rwlock must point to an initialized cups_rwlock_t.
Each successful write lock must be paired with a corresponding cupsRWUnlock by the same thread.
May block until all readers and writers have released the lock (typical RW-lock behavior).

functions.name: cupsRWUnlock
functions.description: Releases a previously acquired read or write lock.
requirements: rwlock must point to an initialized cups_rwlock_t.
The calling thread must currently hold a read or write lock on rwlock.
Each unlock must correspond to a prior successful cupsRWLockRead or cupsRWLockWrite by the same thread.

functions.name: cupsThreadCancel
functions.description: Requests cancellation of the specified thread. Actual cancellation behavior depends on the target thread's cancellation state and points (platform/library-specific).
requirements: thread must be a valid cups_thread_t (not CUPS_THREAD_INVALID).
Caller should ensure the target thread is joinable or otherwise arranged to terminate safely after cancellation (typical requirement).
Subsequent synchronization (join or detach) should be performed to avoid resource leaks.

functions.name: cupsThreadCreate
functions.description: Creates a new thread that begins execution at func(arg). Returns a thread identifier or CUPS_THREAD_INVALID on failure. The function pointer type is cups_thread_func_t and must return a void* result.
requirements: func must be a valid function pointer with signature compatible with cups_thread_func_t.
Any data pointed to by arg must remain valid for the duration of its use by the new thread.
Caller must check the returned cups_thread_t for validity (compare against CUPS_THREAD_INVALID) before using it.
The created thread must eventually be joined via cupsThreadWait or detached via cupsThreadDetach to avoid resource leaks.

functions.name: cupsThreadDetach
functions.description: Marks a thread as detached so that its resources are automatically released on termination and it cannot be waited on.
requirements: thread must be a valid cups_thread_t.
Do not call cupsThreadWait on a detached thread.
Do not detach a thread that has already been detached or already joined (undefined behavior).

functions.name: cupsThreadWait
functions.description: Waits for the specified thread to terminate and returns the thread's exit value (the value returned by its start function).
requirements: thread must be a valid cups_thread_t referring to a joinable (non-detached) thread.
Must not be called more than once for the same thread.
The caller should ensure the thread was created successfully (not CUPS_THREAD_INVALID).

functions.name: cupsDirClose
functions.description: Closes a directory handle previously opened with cupsDirOpen and releases associated resources. Use this after finishing enumeration of entries.
requirements: dp must be a non-NULL pointer returned by cupsDirOpen.
dp must not be used after it has been closed by cupsDirClose.
Calling cupsDirClose is required to release resources when you are done with the directory handle.

functions.name: cupsDirOpen
functions.description: Opens the specified directory for enumeration and returns an opaque handle used with cupsDirRead and cupsDirRewind. Intended as a CUPS abstraction similar to opendir.
requirements: directory must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string path.
directory should refer to an existing directory that the process can access (read/execute as required by the platform).
The returned handle (if non-NULL) must be closed with cupsDirClose.
If the function returns NULL, the caller should treat it as a failure to open the directory; specific error reporting is not defined here.

functions.name: cupsDirRead
functions.description: Reads the next entry from an open directory handle and returns a pointer to a cups_dentry_t containing the filename and stat info. Returns NULL on end-of-directory or error. Used repeatedly after cupsDirOpen until no more entries are available.
requirements: dp must be a non-NULL directory handle returned by cupsDirOpen and not yet closed.
Call repeatedly to iterate entries; a NULL return indicates end-of-directory or an error.

The returned cups_dentry_t pointer is owned by the directory iterator; the caller must not free it. Its lifetime may be only until the next call to cupsDirRead or until dp is closed (exact ownership semantics are not specified here).
Do not access the returned pointer after cupsDirClose is called on dp.

functions.name: cupsDirRewind
functions.description: Resets the position of the directory stream to the beginning so that subsequent calls to cupsDirRead enumerate entries from the start again.
requirements: dp must be a non-NULL directory handle previously returned by cupsDirOpen and not yet closed.
After rewinding, any previously returned cups_dentry_t pointers should be considered invalid (exact validity not specified).

functions.name: cupsDNSSDCopyComputerName
functions.description: Copies the current DNS-SD computer name associated with the given DNS-SD context into the supplied buffer, returning the buffer on success or NULL on error. Use when you need the user-friendly/mDNS computer name for display or service registration. The copy includes a terminating NUL and truncates/returns NULL if the buffer is too small.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid cups_dnssd_t* previously returned by cupsDNSSDNew and not yet deleted.
buffer must be a writable, non-NULL pointer.
bufsize must be greater than 0 and large enough to hold the resulting name including the terminating NUL.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect errors.
cb_data provided to cupsDNSSDNew (if any) must remain valid while this function is used, as errors may be reported via the error callback (inferred from API pattern).

functions.name: cupsDNSSDCopyHostName
functions.description: Copies the current DNS-SD host name for the given DNS-SD context into the provided buffer, returning the buffer on success or NULL on error. Use to obtain the mDNS host name (e.g., hostname.local.) for registrations, logging, or diagnostics.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid cups_dnssd_t* from cupsDNSSDNew and not deleted.
buffer must be a writable, non-NULL pointer.
bufsize must be > 0 and sufficient for the hostname plus terminating NUL.
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect errors.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDDelete
functions.description: Destroys and frees a DNS-SD context created by cupsDNSSDNew, cancelling any outstanding operations associated with it. Call when finished with DNS-SD operations to release resources.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid pointer returned by cupsDNSSDNew.
Must not be called more than once for the same dnssd handle.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDGetConfigChanges
functions.description: Returns a counter or number of configuration changes detected by the DNS-SD context (e.g., host/network changes). Intended for callers that need to detect when DNS-SD relevant configuration changes occur. Exact semantics of the returned value are not documented here; treat non-zero or increasing values as indicative of changes.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid cups_dnssd_t* from cupsDNSSDNew and not deleted.
Caller should not assume specific units/semantics beyond it being a count; behavior details are unknown from this header and should be verified against implementation/documentation.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDNew
functions.description: Creates a new DNS-SD context used to perform browse, query, resolve, and service registration operations. Optional error callback can be provided to receive asynchronous error messages.
requirements: error_cb may be NULL or a valid function pointer that remains callable for the lifetime of the context (NULL allowance is inferred; actual requirement unknown).
cb_data is an opaque pointer passed to error_cb; it must remain valid for the lifetime of the context if error_cb is non-NULL.
The returned context must be released with cupsDNSSDDelete when no longer needed.
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect allocation/initialization failure.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDBrowseDelete
functions.description: Cancels and frees a DNS-SD browse operation created by cupsDNSSDBrowseNew.
requirements: browser must be a valid handle returned by cupsDNSSDBrowseNew.
Must not be called more than once for the same browser handle.
Associated callbacks will no longer be invoked after deletion.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDBrowseGetContext
functions.description: Returns the DNS-SD context associated with a browse handle. Useful for retrieving the parent context from a callback.
requirements: browser must be a valid handle from cupsDNSSDBrowseNew and not deleted.
Caller must not free or modify the returned context via this function; ownership remains with the creator.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDBrowseNew
functions.signature: cups_dnssd_browse_t *cupsDNSSDBrowseNew(cups_dnssd_t *dnssd, uint32_t if_index, const char *types, const char *domain, cups_dnssd_browse_cb_t browse_cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Starts a DNS-SD browse for the given service types within the specified domain and interface, invoking browse_cb for discovered/removed services and events. Returns a handle to manage the browse operation.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid cups_dnssd_t* from cupsDNSSDNew.
if_index may be a system interface index or a special value such as CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_ANY or CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_LOCAL (per constants defined in this header).
types must be a non-NULL service type string (e.g., "_ipp._tcp"), possibly allowing multiple types per implementation; exact formatting beyond DNS-SD conventions is not specified here.
domain must be a valid domain string; whether NULL selects a default domain is unknown from this header.
browse_cb must be a non-NULL callback function pointer that remains valid for the lifetime of the browse.
cb_data is passed to the callback and must remain valid for the lifetime of the browse.
The returned handle must be released with cupsDNSSDBrowseDelete.
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect failure.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDQueryDelete
functions.description: Cancels and frees a DNS record query created by cupsDNSSDQueryNew.
requirements: query must be a valid handle returned by cupsDNSSDQueryNew.
Must not be called more than once for the same query handle.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDQueryGetContext
functions.description: Returns the DNS-SD context associated with a query handle.
requirements: query must be a valid handle from cupsDNSSDQueryNew and not deleted.
Returned context is not owned by the caller and must not be freed here.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDQueryNew
functions.signature: cups_dnssd_query_t *cupsDNSSDQueryNew(cups_dnssd_t *dnssd, uint32_t if_index, const char *fullname, uint16_t rrtype, cups_dnssd_query_cb_t query_cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Starts a DNS query for a specific record type (rrtype) for the given full DNS-SD service name, invoking query_cb with answers or events. Returns a handle for the ongoing query.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid cups_dnssd_t* from cupsDNSSDNew.
if_index may be a system interface index or a special value like CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_ANY or CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_LOCAL.
fullname must be a non-NULL, fully-qualified service instance name (e.g., "Name._service._tcp.local.").
rrtype must be a valid DNS record type; use values from cups_dnssd_rrtype_t or numeric equivalents.
query_cb must be non-NULL and remain valid for the lifetime of the query.
cb_data must remain valid for the lifetime of the query.
The returned handle must be deleted with cupsDNSSDQueryDelete.
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect failure.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDResolveDelete
functions.description: Cancels and frees a resolve operation created by cupsDNSSDResolveNew.
requirements: res must be a valid handle returned by cupsDNSSDResolveNew.
Must not be called more than once for the same resolve handle.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDResolveGetContext
functions.description: Returns the DNS-SD context associated with a resolve handle.
requirements: res must be a valid cups_dnssd_resolve_t* created by cupsDNSSDResolveNew and not deleted.
Returned context is not owned by the caller and must not be freed here.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDResolveNew
functions.signature: cups_dnssd_resolve_t *cupsDNSSDResolveNew(cups_dnssd_t *dnssd, uint32_t if_index, const char *name, const char *type, const char *domain, cups_dnssd_resolve_cb_t resolve_cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Initiates resolution of a discovered service instance (name/type/domain) to obtain target host, port, and TXT key/value pairs. Invokes resolve_cb with results and events. Returns a handle to manage the resolve operation.
requirements: dnssd must be a valid cups_dnssd_t* from cupsDNSSDNew.
if_index may be a system interface index or CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_ANY/CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_LOCAL.
name, type, and domain must be non-NULL strings that together identify the service instance.
resolve_cb must be non-NULL and remain valid for the lifetime of the resolve.

The returned handle must be released with cupsDNSSDResolveDelete.
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect failure.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServiceAdd
functions.signature: bool cupsDNSSDServiceAdd(cups_dnssd_service_t *service, const char *types, const char *domain, const char *host, uint16_t port, size_t num_txt, cups_option_t *txt);
functions.description: Adds a service record (type/domain/host/port/TXT) to a DNS-SD service registration handle, preparing it for publication. Returns true on success, false on failure. Use to configure one or more advertised service types and their attributes before publishing.
requirements: service must be a valid handle returned by cupsDNSSDServiceNew.
types must be a non-NULL DNS-SD service type string (e.g., "_ipp._tcp"); exact formatting for multiple types (if supported) is unspecified here.
domain must be a valid domain string; whether NULL selects a default domain is unknown from this header.
host must be a valid target host name; whether NULL implies the local host is unknown from this header.
port must be a valid TCP/UDP port number in the range 1–65535; byte order requirements are unknown from this header (likely host order; unspecified).
If num_txt > 0, txt must point to an array of num_txt cups_option_t entries describing TXT keys/values; if num_txt == 0, txt may be NULL (inferred from common CUPS option patterns).
Caller must check the boolean return value for success/failure.
Any dynamically allocated cups_option_t array provided by the caller remains owned by the caller.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServiceDelete
functions.description: Deletes a DNS-SD service registration handle created by cupsDNSSDServiceNew, cancelling publication if active and freeing resources.
requirements: service must be a valid handle returned by cupsDNSSDServiceNew.
Must not be called more than once for the same service handle.
All ongoing publications associated with this handle will stop upon deletion.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServiceGetContext
functions.description: Returns the DNS-SD context associated with a service registration handle.
requirements: service must be a valid cups_dnssd_service_t* created by cupsDNSSDServiceNew and not deleted.
Returned context is not owned by the caller and must not be freed here.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServiceGetName
functions.description: Returns the service instance name associated with a service registration handle, typically the name provided to cupsDNSSDServiceNew.
requirements: service must be a valid handle from cupsDNSSDServiceNew and not deleted.
The returned pointer remains valid as long as the service handle is valid; the caller must not free or modify it (inferred).

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServiceNew
functions.signature: cups_dnssd_service_t *cupsDNSSDServiceNew(cups_dnssd_t *dnssd, uint32_t if_index, const char *name, cups_dnssd_service_cb_t cb, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Creates a new DNS-SD service registration handle for a given interface and service instance name. A callback can be provided to receive registration events (e.g., added, collision, errors).
requirements: dnssd must be a valid cups_dnssd_t* from cupsDNSSDNew.
if_index may be a system interface index or CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_ANY/CUPS_DNSSD_IF_INDEX_LOCAL.
name must be a non-NULL service instance name string.
cb must be a non-NULL callback that remains valid for the lifetime of the service handle.
cb_data must remain valid for the lifetime of the service handle.
The returned handle must be deleted with cupsDNSSDServiceDelete when no longer needed.
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect failure.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServicePublish
functions.description: Publishes (announces) the configured DNS-SD service(s) associated with the service handle. Returns true on success, false on failure.
requirements: service must be a valid handle created by cupsDNSSDServiceNew.
Service should have been configured (e.g., via cupsDNSSDServiceAdd) before publishing; exact preconditions are not fully specified here.
Caller must check the boolean return value for success/failure.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDServiceSetLocation
functions.description: Sets the location metadata (e.g., a geo: URI) for the service registration, to be advertised via DNS-SD TXT or related metadata as supported. Returns true on success, false on failure.
requirements: service must be a valid handle returned by cupsDNSSDServiceNew.
geo_uri must be a non-NULL, valid location string; exact format requirements are not specified here (commonly a RFC 5870 geo: URI, but unspecified in this header).
Caller must check the boolean return value for success/failure.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDAssembleFullName
functions.signature: bool cupsDNSSDAssembleFullName(char *fullname, size_t fullsize, const char *name, const char *type, const char *domain);
functions.description: Constructs a fully-qualified DNS-SD service instance name from separate name, type, and domain components and writes it into fullname. Returns true on success, false if the output buffer is too small or inputs are invalid.
requirements: fullname must be a writable, non-NULL buffer.
fullsize must be > 0 and large enough to hold the assembled full name including terminating NUL.
name, type, and domain must be non-NULL strings following DNS-SD conventions (e.g., type like "_ipp._tcp").
Caller must check the boolean return value for success/failure.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDDecodeTXT
functions.signature: size_t cupsDNSSDDecodeTXT(const unsigned char *txtrec, uint16_t txtlen, cups_option_t **txt);
functions.description: Parses a DNS-SD TXT record byte buffer into an array of cups_option_t key/value pairs. Returns the number of options parsed, or 0 on error. On success, *txt is set to a newly allocated array owned by the caller.
requirements: txtrec must point to a buffer of at least txtlen bytes containing a DNS-SD TXT record in wire format.
txtlen is the length in bytes of txtrec.
txt must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated cups_option_t array on success.
On success, the caller owns the returned array and should free it using cupsFreeOptions(num_options, *txt) (inferred from CUPS option patterns).
Caller must check the returned size and only use *txt when the return value is > 0.

functions.name: cupsDNSSDSeparateFullName
functions.signature: bool cupsDNSSDSeparateFullName(const char *fullname, char *name, size_t namesize, char *type, size_t typesize, char *domain, size_t domainsize);
functions.description: Splits a fully-qualified DNS-SD service instance name into its name, type, and domain components, writing them into the provided buffers. Returns true on success, false if parsing fails or any buffer is too small.
requirements: fullname must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing a full DNS-SD service name.
name, type, and domain must be writable buffers; each must be non-NULL if its corresponding size is greater than 0.
namesize, typesize, and domainsize must be > 0 and large enough to hold the corresponding component including terminating NUL.
Caller must check the boolean return value for success/failure.

functions.name: cupsArrayAdd
functions.description: Adds an element to a CUPS sorted array. Intended to insert the element according to the array’s comparison semantics and update internal iteration state. Returns true on success, false on failure.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t* previously created by cupsArrayNew or cupsArrayNewStrings and not yet deleted.
e must be a valid pointer compatible with the array’s element type and comparison/copy/free callbacks (if any).
Behavior when adding duplicate elements is unspecified in this header (unknown whether duplicates are allowed).
Thread-safety is not documented; callers should provide external synchronization if needed (unknown).

functions.name: cupsArrayAddStrings
functions.signature: extern bool cupsArrayAddStrings(cups_array_t *a, const char *s, char delim);
functions.description: Splits the input string s using the delimiter character delim and adds each token as an element to the array. Intended for arrays of strings. Returns true if all additions succeed, false otherwise.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t* created by cupsArrayNew (with string-compatible callbacks) or cupsArrayNewStrings and not yet deleted.
s must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
delim specifies the separator character; tokens are determined by occurrences of this character. Exact handling of consecutive delimiters and empty tokens is not specified (unknown).
Element ownership/copying depends on the array’s copy/free callbacks; if the array does not copy strings, the lifetime of s-derived tokens must outlive the array (unknown exact behavior).

functions.name: cupsArrayClear
functions.description: Removes all elements from the array, leaving the array object allocated and reusable. If a free callback was provided at creation, it will be used to release each element.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t* and not NULL.
After clearing, iteration state may be reset (exact specifics are not documented; unknown).

functions.name: cupsArrayDelete
functions.description: Destroys the array and releases associated resources. If a free callback was provided, it is called for each stored element before deallocation.
requirements: a must be a cups_array_t* previously created by cupsArrayNew or cupsArrayNewStrings; passing NULL is not specified (unknown).
After this call, a and any iterators derived from it must not be used.

functions.name: cupsArrayDup
functions.description: Creates and returns a duplicate of the array. The duplicate contains copies of elements if a copy callback was defined; otherwise it likely copies element pointers. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t* and not NULL.
Resulting array must be deleted with cupsArrayDelete when no longer needed.
Exact element duplication semantics depend on the original array’s copy callback (unknown if deep copy occurs without a copy callback).

functions.name: cupsArrayFind
functions.description: Searches the array for an element equal to e using the array’s comparison function and returns the stored matching element pointer, or NULL if not found.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
e must be a pointer value comparable by the array’s comparison callback.
Comparison semantics (equality, ordering) are determined by the comparator supplied to cupsArrayNew; behavior without a comparator is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: cupsArrayGetCount
functions.description: Returns the number of elements currently stored in the array.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Return value fits in size_t; for empty arrays returns 0.

functions.name: cupsArrayGetCurrent
functions.description: Returns the element at the array’s current iterator position, or NULL if there is no current element.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
A current position is typically established by cupsArrayGetFirst, cupsArrayGetLast, cupsArrayGetNext, or cupsArrayGetPrev; behavior before any iterator call is not specified (unknown).

functions.name: cupsArrayGetElement
functions.description: Returns the element at zero-based index n, or NULL if n is out of range.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
n must be less than cupsArrayGetCount(a); behavior for n >= count is returning NULL (inferred by common conventions; exact guarantee not explicitly stated).

functions.name: cupsArrayGetFirst
functions.description: Positions the array’s iterator at the first element and returns it, or returns NULL if the array is empty.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Subsequent calls to cupsArrayGetNext iterate forward from this position.

functions.name: cupsArrayGetIndex
functions.description: Returns the zero-based index of the current iterator position. The sentinel used when no current element exists is not documented here (unknown; often SIZE_MAX).
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
A current position is typically established via iteration helpers (GetFirst/GetNext/GetLast/GetPrev).
Caller must handle the case where there is no current element (returned value when invalid is unspecified here).

functions.name: cupsArrayGetInsert
functions.description: Returns the index at which the last insertion would occur or did occur. Exact semantics are not documented in this header; commonly used to learn the insertion point from a previous search/insert operation.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Meaningful only after operations that set an insertion context (e.g., a failed find or an insert); exact prerequisites and return when unset are unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: cupsArrayGetLast
functions.description: Positions the iterator at the last element and returns it, or NULL if the array is empty.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Subsequent calls to cupsArrayGetPrev iterate backward from this position.

functions.name: cupsArrayGetNext
functions.description: Advances the iterator forward and returns the next element, or NULL if at the end.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Typically call cupsArrayGetFirst before the first call to GetNext.
Modifications to the array during iteration may invalidate the iterator (behavior not documented; unknown).

functions.name: cupsArrayGetPrev
functions.description: Moves the iterator backward and returns the previous element, or NULL if at the beginning.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Typically call cupsArrayGetLast before the first call to GetPrev.
Modifications to the array during iteration may invalidate the iterator (behavior not documented; unknown).

functions.name: cupsArrayGetUserData
functions.description: Returns the user data pointer associated with the array, as provided when the array was created (cupsArrayNew).
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
User data comes from the d parameter of cupsArrayNew; arrays created with cupsArrayNewStrings may have NULL user data (unspecified).

functions.name: cupsArrayInsert
functions.description: Inserts an element into the array at the position determined by the array’s ordering, potentially using a precomputed insertion point. Returns true on success, false on failure. The distinction between Insert and Add is not specified here (unknown).
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
e must be a valid pointer compatible with the array’s callbacks.
Duplicate handling and stability are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: cupsArrayNew
functions.signature: extern cups_array_t *cupsArrayNew(cups_array_cb_t f, void *d, cups_ahash_cb_t hf, size_t hsize, cups_acopy_cb_t cf, cups_afree_cb_t ff);
functions.description: Creates a new CUPS sorted array. The comparator f defines ordering and equality. d is an opaque user data pointer available to callbacks and retrievable via cupsArrayGetUserData. Optional callbacks include an element hash function hf (to enable/optimize lookups), an element copy function cf, and an element free function ff. hsize provides the hash table size when hashing is used. Returns a pointer to the new array, or NULL on failure.
requirements: f defines the array’s sort and equality semantics; it should impose a consistent strict weak ordering (inferred from typical comparator contracts; exact requirement not documented).
If hf is non-NULL, hsize should be a positive nonzero value appropriate for the hash table size; behavior when hf is provided with hsize==0 is not documented (unknown).
cf, if provided, must return a valid element copy compatible with ff; ff must safely free elements produced by cf or added directly.
d is stored and later returned by cupsArrayGetUserData; it is not managed by the array.
Returned array must be deleted with cupsArrayDelete.
NULL allowances for f, hf, cf, ff are not fully specified (unknown).

functions.name: cupsArrayNewStrings
functions.description: Creates a new array populated from the delimited string s. The array is set up for string elements. Returns the new array on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
delim specifies the token separator; exact handling of empty tokens and whitespace is not specified (unknown).
The resulting array must be deleted with cupsArrayDelete when no longer needed.
String storage/duplication semantics are not fully documented here (unknown).

functions.name: cupsArrayRemove
functions.description: Removes the element equal to e from the array, if present, using the array’s comparison semantics. Returns true if an element was removed, false otherwise.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
e must be a pointer comparable by the array’s comparator.
If a free callback was provided, it will be used to release the removed element.

functions.name: cupsArrayRestore
functions.description: Restores a previously saved iterator position and returns the current element at that position, or NULL if there is no saved state or it is invalid. Intended to pair with cupsArraySave.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
Should be called after a successful cupsArraySave; nested save/restore depth and behavior are not documented (unknown).
Array modifications between save and restore may affect the restored position (behavior not specified; unknown).

functions.name: cupsArraySave
functions.description: Saves the current iterator position so it can be restored later via cupsArrayRestore. Returns true on success, false on failure.
requirements: a must be a valid cups_array_t*.
A current iterator position should exist before calling (e.g., after GetFirst/GetLast/iteration); exact behavior when no current element exists is not documented (unknown).
The number of saved positions supported (nesting) is not specified (unknown).

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Use safe printable ASCII excluding NUL; include URL-ish and token chars
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./:@?&=%,+#|~ "
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_token(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-_."
    s = ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    if not s:
        s = "x"
    return s

def _rand_pwg_media_keyword(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common valid PWG media names plus random fallback
    common = [
        "iso_a4_210x297mm",
        "na_letter_8.5x11in",
        "iso_a3_297x420mm",
        "na_legal_8.5x14in",
        "iso_a5_148x210mm",
    ]
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        return r.choice(common)
    # Fallback: prefix_name_WxHunits
    units = r.choice(["mm", "in"]) 
    if units == "mm":
        w = r.randrange(50, 420)
        h = r.randrange(50, 594)
        return f"iso_custom_{w}x{h}mm"
    else:
        w = r.randrange(2, 18)
        h = r.randrange(2, 24)
        return f"na_custom_{w}.{r.randrange(0,10)}x{h}.{r.randrange(0,10)}in"

def _rand_http_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Ensure starts with '/'
    segs = [ _rand_token(r, 1, r.randint(3,10)) for _ in range(r.randint(1,4)) ]
    return "/" + "/".join(segs)

def _rand_uri(r: random.Random) -> str:
    scheme = r.choice(["http", "https", "ipp"]) 
    host = _rand_token(r, 3, 12)
    tld = r.choice(["local", "test", "example", "lan"]) 
    port = ":%d" % r.randrange(1, 65535) if r.random() < 0.3 else ""
    path = _rand_http_path(r)
    return f"{scheme}://{host}.{tld}{port}{path}"

def _rand_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a simple relative filename to be used where a fuzz file is created by harness
    base = _rand_token(r, 3, 10)
    ext = r.choice([".txt", ".bin", ".dat", ".json", ".ipp"]) 
    return base + ext

def _kv_options_string(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build comma-separated key=value pairs likely parsable by cupsParseOptions/cupsFormDecode
    pairs: List[str] = []
    # include media and copies commonly used
    pairs.append(f"media={_rand_pwg_media_keyword(r)}")
    pairs.append(f"copies={r.randint(1, 10)}")
    # add 0-3 extra pairs
    for _ in range(r.randint(0,3)):
        k = _rand_token(r, 2, 12)
        # sometimes integer, sometimes token
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            v = str(r.randint(0, 1000))
        else:
            v = _rand_token(r, 1, 16)
        pairs.append(f"{k}={v}")
    return ",".join(pairs)

def _dns_sd_txt_wire(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a valid DNS-SD TXT record wire format: len(<=255) followed by bytes
    entries: List[bytes] = []
    # Ensure at least one valid entry like txtvers=1
    entries.append(b"txtvers=1")
    # Add 0-4 additional k=v short entries
    for i in range(r.randint(0,4)):
        key = f"k{i}".encode()
        val = _rand_token(r, 1, 8).encode()
        entries.append(key + b"=" + val)
    out = bytearray()
    for e in entries:
        l = len(e)
        if l > 255:
            e = e[:255]
            l = 255
        out.append(l)
        out.extend(e)
    return bytes(out)

def _base64_like(r: random.Random, urlsafe: bool) -> str:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ("-_" if urlsafe else "+/")
    s = ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(r.randint(8, 64)))
    # Add padding sometimes for standard b64
    if not urlsafe and r.random() < 0.7:
        pad = r.choice(["", "=", "=="]) 
        s += pad
    return s

def _jwt_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a syntactically valid JWS Compact: header.payload.signature with base64url
    def seg(obj: str) -> str:
        # crude base64url without padding to look valid
        raw = obj.encode()
        # simple transform to URL-safe set
        table = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_"
        return ''.join(table[b % len(table)] for b in raw)
    header = '{"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}'
    payload = '{"sub":"' + _rand_token(r,3,10) + '","exp":' + str(r.randint(1_700_000_000, 1_900_000_000)) + '}'
    sig = _rand_token(r, 16, 48)
    return seg(header) + "." + seg(payload) + "." + seg(sig)

def _json_small(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Small valid JSON object with 1-3 members
    n = r.randint(1,3)
    items = []
    for _ in range(n):
        k = _rand_token(r, 1, 8)
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            v = '"' + _rand_ascii(r,1,10).replace('"','') + '"'
        else:
            v = str(r.randint(-1000,1000))
        items.append('"%s":%s' % (k, v))
    return "{" + ",".join(items) + "}"

def _language_tag(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # BCP47-ish tags
    primary = r.choice(["en","fr","de","es","pt","zh","ja","ko","it","nl"]) 
    region = r.choice(["US","GB","DE","FR","ES","BR","CN","JP"]) 
    return primary + "_" + region

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Compose multiple concatenated NUL-terminated strings in one buffer, to satisfy many FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
    # Strategy: include a mixture of values commonly expected by stubs.
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1. Printer/destination names and instances
    parts.append(_rand_token(r, 3, 12).encode() + b"\0")
    parts.append((_rand_token(r, 3, 8) if r.random()<0.5 else "").encode() + b"\0")

    # 2. Media related strings (names, color, source, type)
    parts.append(_rand_pwg_media_keyword(r).encode() + b"\0")
    parts.append(_rand_token(r, 3, 10).encode() + b"\0")  # color
    parts.append(_rand_token(r, 3, 10).encode() + b"\0")  # source
    parts.append(_rand_token(r, 3, 12).encode() + b"\0")  # type

    # 3. HTTP method/resource
    parts.append(r.choice([b"GET", b"POST", b"PUT", b"DELETE"]) + b"\0")
    parts.append(_rand_http_path(r).encode() + b"\0")

    # 4. URIs and filenames
    parts.append(_rand_uri(r).encode() + b"\0")
    parts.append(_rand_filename(r).encode() + b"\0")

    # 5. Options key/value and option strings
    parts.append(_rand_token(r, 2, 12).encode() + b"\0")
    parts.append(_rand_token(r, 1, 16).encode() + b"\0")
    parts.append(_kv_options_string(r).encode() + b"\0")

    # 6. Credentials/common names/paths
    parts.append(_rand_token(r, 3, 10).encode() + b"\0")  # common name
    parts.append(_rand_token(r, 1, 8).encode() + b"\0")   # creds id
    parts.append(_rand_token(r, 1, 8).encode() + b"\0")   # key id

    # 7. JSON and JWT inputs
    parts.append(_json_small(r).encode() + b"\0")

    # 8. Base64 data (std and url-safe)

    # 11. IPP attribute names and values
    parts.append(_rand_token(r, 3, 15).encode() + b"\0")
    parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 20).encode() + b"\0")

    # 12. OAuth-like inputs
    parts.append(("https://auth.local/" + _rand_token(r,3,12)).encode() + b"\0")
    parts.append(("https://resource.local/" + _rand_token(r,3,12)).encode() + b"\0")

    parts.append(("https://app.local/cb/" + _rand_token(r,3,10)).encode() + b"\0")

    # 13. JSON keys/values for cups_json API
    parts.append(_rand_token(r,1,8).encode() + b"\0")

    # 14. Misc strings for headers/fields/auth/cookies

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path string
# We generate a bytes buffer that the harness will use via FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# Goals:
# - Produce plausible, valid paths for files and directories.
# - Cover absolute and relative paths, nested subdirs, dot/dotdot, and varied extensions.
# - Sometimes include credential-like filenames used by CUPS (certs/keys/CSR), JSON, IPP text, etc.
# - Keep under 4096 bytes.
# - Seeded randomness.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."
EXTS = [
    "crt", "cer", "pem", "key", "csr", "json", "ipp", "txt", "conf", "ppd",
    "dat", "bin", "log"
]

# Common credential-related base names to exercise cups*Credentials* APIs
CRED_NAMES = [
    "cups", "server", "client", "root", "intermediate", "tls", "default",
    "private", "public", "ca", "cert", "key", "request"
]

DIR_HINTS = [
    ".", "..", "tmp", "run", "var", "etc", "cups", "ssl", "spool", "cache", "keys",
    "certs", "requests", "conf", "profiles"
]

# Build a path with components chosen to be valid on POSIX and Windows alike (avoid reserved characters)
def _rand_component(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n)).strip()
    # Ensure not empty after strip; fallback
    if not s:
        s = "x"
    # Avoid trailing spaces or dots that Windows dislikes; trim but keep something
    s = s.rstrip(" .") or "x"
    return s

def _choose_base_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Sometimes pick a semantic credential name
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        left = r.choice(CRED_NAMES)
        right = r.choice(["cert", "key", "csr", "bundle", "chain", "pub", "priv"]) if r.random() < 0.6 else r.choice(CRED_NAMES)
        base = f"{left}-{right}"
    else:
        base = _rand_component(r, 3, 12)
    # Append an extension
    if r.random() < 0.9:
        ext = r.choice(EXTS)
    else:
        ext = _rand_component(r, 2, 4)
    return f"{base}.{ext}"

def _build_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Decide absolute vs relative
    absolute = r.random() < 0.5
    # Decide platform style: POSIX or Windows-like (but keep it usable on POSIX fuzz hosts)
    win_style = r.random() < 0.2

    comps: List[str] = []

    # Optionally start within a common directory structure
    depth = r.randint(0, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            comps.append(r.choice(DIR_HINTS))
        else:
            comps.append(_rand_component(r, 1, 10))

    # Sprinkle dot or dot-dot occasionally
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        comps.insert(r.randint(0, len(comps)), r.choice([".", ".."]))

    # Final filename
    leaf = _choose_base_filename(r) if r.random() < 0.8 else _rand_component(r, 3, 12)

    # Construct path
    if win_style and absolute:
        drive = r.choice(list(string.ascii_letters)) + ":"
        sep = "\\"  # we will normalize to forward slashes for cross-platform, but keep variant sometimes
        path = drive + sep + sep.join(comps + [leaf]) if comps else drive + sep + leaf
        # Convert backslashes to forward slashes with some probability to be more portable
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            path = path.replace("\\", "/")
    else:
        sep = "/"
        prefix = "/" if absolute else ""
        path = prefix + sep.join([c for c in comps if c] + [leaf]) if leaf else prefix + sep.join([c for c in comps if c])
        if not path:
            path = "."  # fallback

    return path

def _maybe_directory_path(r: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    # Some stubs expect directories (e.g., cupsSetServerCredentials path may be a dir). Provide those sometimes.
    if r.random() < 0.35:
        # Replace leaf with a directory name
        parts = base.replace("\\", "/").split("/")
        if parts:
            parts[-1] = r.choice(DIR_HINTS)
        path = "/".join(p for p in parts if p)
        # Randomly append a trailing slash
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            path += "/"
        return path
    return base

def _add_variations(r: random.Random, path: str) -> str:
    # Add common variations to trigger different behaviors
    p = path
    # Sometimes choose just "." or a simple absolute root
    if r.random() < 0.05:
        return "/" if path.startswith("/") else "."
    # Append an extra credential-ish basename sometimes to create deeper paths
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        p = p.rstrip("/") + "/" + _choose_base_filename(r)
    # Occasionally add a suffix like ".old" or ".bak"
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        p += ".bak" if r.random() < 0.5 else ".old"
    return p

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build multiple candidate paths and choose one to pack into the buffer set.
    paths: List[str] = []
    count = r.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(count):
        p = _build_path(r)
        p = _maybe_directory_path(r, p)
        p = _add_variations(r, p)
        paths.append(p)

    # Join multiple paths separated by NUL to allow consumers that pick first NUL-terminated string
    # to get a valid path, while others may read subsequent ones for different fields.
    # Ensure total size <= 4096.
    blob = "\x00".join(paths)
    data = blob.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import struct
import zlib

# Data model: Generate valid and interesting IPP and IPP-like text files as arbitrary file data.
# Outputs are <= 4096 bytes and self-contained.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# IPP group tags
IPP_TAG_OPERATION = 0x01
IPP_TAG_JOB = 0x02
IPP_TAG_END = 0x03
IPP_TAG_PRINTER = 0x04  # missing previously; define proper group tag value

# IPP value tags
IPP_TAG_INTEGER = 0x21
IPP_TAG_BOOLEAN = 0x22
IPP_TAG_ENUM = 0x23
IPP_TAG_TEXT = 0x41
IPP_TAG_NAME = 0x42
IPP_TAG_KEYWORD = 0x44
IPP_TAG_URI = 0x45
IPP_TAG_CHARSET = 0x47
IPP_TAG_LANGUAGE = 0x48

# Helper: length-prefixed string in IPP (2-byte big-endian length followed by bytes)
def _ipp_str(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H", len(s)) + s


def _ipp_attr(tag: int, name: str, value_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    return bytes([tag]) + _ipp_str(name.encode("utf-8")) + _ipp_str(value_bytes)


def _ipp_attr_text(tag: int, name: str, text: str) -> bytes:
    return _ipp_attr(tag, name, text.encode("utf-8"))


def _ipp_attr_int(tag: int, name: str, val: int) -> bytes:
    return (
        bytes([tag])
        + _ipp_str(name.encode("utf-8"))
        + struct.pack(">H", 4)
        + struct.pack(">i", val)
    )


def _ipp_attr_bool(name: str, b: bool) -> bytes:
    return (
        bytes([IPP_TAG_BOOLEAN])
        + _ipp_str(name.encode("utf-8"))
        + struct.pack(">H", 1)
        + (b"\x01" if b else b"\x00")
    )


def _ipp_header(version=(2, 0), op_or_status=0x000B, request_id=1) -> bytes:
    ver = bytes([version[0], version[1]])
    return ver + struct.pack(">H", op_or_status) + struct.pack(">I", request_id)


def make_binary_ipp_request(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a minimal but valid IPP request: Get-Printer-Attributes (0x000B)
    req_id = rng.randrange(1, 0x7FFFFFFF)
    version = (2, rng.choice([0, 1]))
    buf = _ipp_header(version, 0x000B, req_id)
    parts = [buf, bytes([IPP_TAG_OPERATION])]
    parts.append(_ipp_attr_text(IPP_TAG_CHARSET, "attributes-charset", "utf-8"))
    parts.append(
        _ipp_attr_text(
            IPP_TAG_LANGUAGE,
            "attributes-natural-language",
            rng.choice(["en-us", "de", "fr", "ja"]),
        )
    )
    uname = rng.choice(["fuzz", "lp", "testuser", "alice", "bob"])
    parts.append(_ipp_attr_text(IPP_TAG_NAME, "requesting-user-name", uname))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(
            _ipp_attr_text(IPP_TAG_URI, "printer-uri", "ipp://localhost/printers/test")
        )
    else:
        parts.append(
            _ipp_attr_text(IPP_TAG_KEYWORD, "document-format", rng.choice(["application/pdf", "application/postscript", "image/pwg-raster"]))
        )
    parts.append(_ipp_attr_int(IPP_TAG_ENUM, "copies-supported", rng.randrange(1, 100)))
    parts.append(_ipp_attr_bool("ipp-attribute-fidelity", rng.choice([True, False])))
    parts.append(bytes([IPP_TAG_END]))
    data = b"".join(parts)
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]


def make_binary_ipp_response(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Successful response (0x0000), include operation attrs and a printer attribute block
    req_id = rng.randrange(1, 0x7FFFFFFF)
    version = (2, rng.choice([0, 1]))
    buf = _ipp_header(version, 0x0000, req_id)
    parts = [buf, bytes([IPP_TAG_OPERATION])]
    parts.append(_ipp_attr_text(IPP_TAG_CHARSET, "attributes-charset", "utf-8"))
    parts.append(
        _ipp_attr_text(
            IPP_TAG_LANGUAGE,
            "attributes-natural-language",
            rng.choice(["en-us", "es", "it"]),
        )
    )
    parts.append(_ipp_attr_text(IPP_TAG_TEXT, "status-message", rng.choice(["ok", "successful-ok"])))
    # Printer group
    parts.append(bytes([IPP_TAG_PRINTER]))
    parts.append(_ipp_attr_text(IPP_TAG_NAME, "printer-name", rng.choice(["Test", "Office", "ColorJet"])))
    parts.append(_ipp_attr_int(IPP_TAG_INTEGER, "printer-state", rng.choice([3, 4, 5])))
    parts.append(_ipp_attr_bool("printer-is-accepting-jobs", True))
    parts.append(bytes([IPP_TAG_END]))
    return b"".join(parts)[:MAX_SIZE]


def make_ipp_text_file(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Textual IPP data file suited for ippFileRead/ReadToken
    lines = []
    lines.append("# IPP data file generated\n")
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        lines.append("{operation-attributes-tag}\n")
        lines.append("attributes-charset charset utf-8\n")
        lines.append(
            f"attributes-natural-language naturalLanguage {rng.choice(['en-us','de','fr','ja'])}\n"
        )
        lines.append(
            f"requesting-user-name nameWithoutLanguage {rng.choice(['fuzz','lp','user','alice'])}\n"
        )
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        lines.append("{job-attributes-tag}\n")
        lines.append(f"copies integer {rng.randrange(1, 50)}\n")
        lines.append(
            f"sides keyword {rng.choice(['one-sided','two-sided-long-edge','two-sided-short-edge'])}\n"
        )
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        lines.append("{printer-attributes-tag}\n")
        lines.append(f"printer-name nameWithoutLanguage {rng.choice(['Test','Office','Color'])}\n")
        lines.append(f"printer-state enum {rng.choice([3,4,5])}\n")
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(2, 6)):
        k = rng.choice(
            ["media", "print-quality", "orientation-requested", "finishings", "output-bin"]
        )
        if k in ("print-quality", "orientation-requested"):
            v = str(rng.choice([3, 4, 5]))
            t = "enum"
        elif k == "finishings":
            v = str(rng.choice([3, 4, 50, 90]))
            t = "enum"
        elif k == "media":
            v = rng.choice(["na_letter_8.5x11in", "iso_a4_210x297mm", "na_legal_8.5x14in"])
            t = "keyword"
        else:
            v = rng.choice(["auto", "upper", "lower"])
            t = "keyword"
        lines.append(f"{k} {t} {v}\n")
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            lines.append(f"# note: {k} set\n")
    text = "".join(lines)
    return text.encode("utf-8")[:MAX_SIZE]


def make_plain_text(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    paras = []
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(3, 12)):
        line = rng.choice(
            [
                "Hello, world!\n",
                "CUPS fuzz input line.\n",
                "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\n",
                f"value={rng.randrange(0,100000)}\n",
                f"name={rng.choice(['alice','bob','charlie'])}\n",
            ]
        )
        paras.append(line)
    return ("".join(paras)).encode("utf-8")[:MAX_SIZE]


def maybe_gzip(rng: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # For arbitrary file data consumers, we keep raw bytes mostly.
    # Optionally compress with zlib to add variety; size remains bounded.
    if not data:
        return data
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        comp = zlib.compress(data, level=rng.choice([1, 6, 9]))
        return comp[:MAX_SIZE]
    return data


def make_small_or_empty(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    options = [b"", b"\n", b"# empty file\n", b"%PDF-1.0\n%%EOF\n", b"{}\n"]
    return rng.choice(options)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        data = make_binary_ipp_request(rng)
    elif choice < 0.5:
        data = make_binary_ipp_response(rng)
    elif choice < 0.7:
        data = make_ipp_text_file(rng)
    elif choice < 0.9:
        data = make_plain_text(rng)
    else:
        data = make_small_or_empty(rng)
    data = maybe_gzip(rng, data)
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]
    return data
